target.title: fix(msteams): bound Bot Framework attachmentInfo JSON response reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Bot Framework personal-chat attachment downloads call `/v3/attachments/{id}` and previously parsed the metadata with unbounded `response.json()`. A hostile or misbehaving endpoint could stream an arbitrarily large JSON body and OOM the gateway process before the attachment view download even starts.

Related open bounded-read work covers MS Teams Graph collection (#98833), Graph upload (#97784), and SSO (#97781), but not the Bot Framework `attachmentInfo` path in `bot-framework.ts`.

Note: Inworld TTS/voices bounded reads are already on `main` (#95416, #98660), so this PR targets the remaining MS Teams gap instead.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route the Bot Framework attachment metadata success path through the shared `readProviderJsonResponse` helper (16 MiB cap, stream cancel on overflow), matching sibling MS Teams Graph/OAuth bounded JSON reads.

## User Impact

No config or API changes. Personal DM / Bot Framework attachment downloads fail closed with a logged warning when attachment metadata JSON exceeds the cap, instead of buffering the full body.

## Evidence

Local proof (worktree `d:\WorkSpace\AI\openclaw-wt-inworld-bound-reads`, branch `fix/msteams-bound-bot-framework-attachmentinfo-json-reads`, commit `30054fe6d6`):

```bash
pnpm test extensions/msteams/src/attachments/bot-framework.test.ts
```

Result: 21/21 tests passed, including `bounds an unbounded attachmentInfo JSON body and cancels the stream` (asserts `response.json()` is not used, stream stops before the 64 MiB test ceiling, overflow surfaces as `JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes`).

Changed files:
- `extensions/msteams/src/attachments/bot-framework.ts` — `readProviderJsonResponse` for attachmentInfo
- `extensions/msteams/src/attachments/bot-framework.test.ts` — bounded-read regression test

target.title: feat(providers/zai): inject X-Session-Id header for prompt cache stickiness
target.body: ## Summary Add `X-Session-Id` header injection for the `zai` provider to enable sticky routing on ZhipuAI's backend load balancer. On a live agent workload (78 GLM-5.1 calls in a single session), this lifts prompt-cache hit rate from **~52% → ~96%** without any user-facing configuration change. Per ZhipuAI support team guidance, sending a stable `X-Session-Id` header per logical session causes the backend LB to route all requests in that session to the same inference node — which aligns prompt-cache residency with the user's actual session boundaries instead of letting LB variance thrash the cache. ## Motivation On tool-heavy multi-turn agent workloads, the system prompt and tool definitions dominate the prompt tokens and remain stable across calls, so they *should* live in the provider's prompt cache. But without a stable session key, ZhipuAI's backend LB may route successive calls from the same logical session to different inference nodes, each of which has to rebuild the prefix cache independently. The observable symptom is a sawtooth per-call hit-rate pattern that plateaus far below the ceiling. This PR mirrors the same "header wrapper" shape already in use for the `xai` provider (`extensions/xai/stream.ts`), so the change is idiomatic and low-risk. ## Design Added `extensions/zai/stream.ts`: - **`createZaiSessionIdHeaderWrapper(baseStreamFn?)`** — stream wrapper that reads `options.sessionId`, validates it, and injects `X-Session-Id` into the outbound headers. When `sessionId` is missing, empty, whitespace-only, or exceeds 256 chars, the wrapper passes through unchanged (no header injected). - **`wrapZaiProviderStream(ctx)`** — provider-level composition. Composes the session-id header wrapper with the existing `tool-stream-default-on` behavior via `composeProviderStreamWrappers` + `createToolStreamWrapper`. Shape mirrors `extensions/xai/stream.ts`. `extensions/zai/index.ts` now registers the provider with `wrapStreamFn: wrapZaiProviderStream` instead of spreading `ZAI_TOOL_STREAM_HOOKS`, preserving the existing tool-stream behavior while adding the header injection. ## Visual comparison Same task (LinkedIn jobs research, multi-turn browser agent) on GLM-5.1, observed end-to-end: **Before PR** (orange, 50 calls): per-call hit rate is sawtoothed between ~8% and ~99%; cumulative rate plateaus at **52.4%**. 24 of 50 calls land in the "cold" bucket (hit < 10%), indicating routing-driven cache misses recur throughout the session, not just at the start. **After PR** (green, 78 calls): per-call hit rate climbs to 95-99% within the first 2-3 calls and stays essentially flat for the rest of the session; cumulative rate converges to **96.27%**. Only **1** cold call (the mandatory first-call warm-up). Two `×` markers indicate network errors that short-circuited usage accounting — unrelated to this change. ## Test plan ### Unit tests (`extensions/zai/stream.test.ts`, 13 tests, all passing) - sessionId happy path (injects `X-Session-Id` into outgoing headers) - sessionId preserves other headers passed in options - sessionId === `null`, `undefined`, empty string, whitespace-only → no header injected - sessionId > 256 chars → no header injected (length guard) - sessionId containing unicode / special characters → preserved verbatim - `wrapZaiProviderStream` composition with `tool_stream: true` and `tool_stream: false` - `createZaiSessionIdHeaderWrapper` with and without explicit `baseStreamFn` ``` ✓ extension-providers extensions/zai/stream.test.ts (13 tests) 16ms Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 13 passed (13) ``` The pre-existing `cache-ttl.test.ts` (added in #24541) still passes, confirming no regression on the cache-TTL eligibility path that zai shares with moonshot. ### Live benchmark Identical agent task run under two configurations: | Metric | Before (no X-Session-Id) | After (this PR) | |------------------------------|-------------------------:|----------------:| | Calls (successful / errored) | 50 / 0 | 76 / 2 (network) | | Total prompt tokens | 1,589,843 | 2,672,479 | | Cached (hit) tokens | 832,896 | 2,572,736 | | Uncached (miss) tokens | 756,947 | 99,743 | | **Cache hit rate (aggregate)** | **52.39%** | **96.27%** | | **Median per-call hit rate** | **79.35%** | **99.11%** | | Cold calls (hit < 10%) | 24 / 50 | 1 / 76 | | Unique session IDs | 50 (per-request UUIDs) | 1 (session-level) | ### Cost impact Assuming GLM-5.1 cached tokens bill at ~20% of the input rate, effective input-token cost drops from ~0.58× nominal to ~0.23× nominal on this workload — **roughly a 60% input-token cost reduction**. ## Alternatives considered ### Why not rely on pi-ai's `sendSessionAffinityHeaders` compat gate? `pi-ai@0.69.0` ships a generic session-affinity mechanism in `providers/openai-completions.js` that, when `compat.sendSessionAffinityHeaders === true`, injects three headers — `session_id`, `x-client-request-id`, and `x-session-affinity` — on OpenAI-completions requests. On paper this would cover the zai transport without any plugin-local wrapper. In practice it doesn't help for this PR: 1. **The gate is default-off and currently unreached.** `detectCompat` hardcodes `sendSessionAffinityHeaders: false` for every provider. Neither pi-ai itself nor `openclaw/main` contains a single write that sets it to `true` — both `grep -rn 'sendSessionAffinityHeaders:\s*true' node_modules/@mariozechner/pi-ai/dist` and `git grep sendSessionAffinityHeaders origin/main` return no matches. Turning it on for zai would be a separate decision in its own right. 2. **The header names don't match.** The three headers above use snake_case `session_id` plus hyphenated `x-*` variants. ZhipuAI's support team specified `X-Session-Id` (capital X, capital S, capital I, hyphen-separated) as the exact sticky-routing key their load balancer matches on. We can't assume the LB accepts the pi-ai variants. 3. **Scope.** Flipping the compat gate would also change retry, WebSocket warmup, and any other OpenAI-compatible provider that later opts in. Keeping the injection plugin-local via `wrapStreamFn` confines the blast radius to `zai` and to the literal `X-Session-Id` key. If ZhipuAI later confirms they also recognize `session_id` / `x-session-affinity`, flipping the compat gate becomes a reasonable follow-up — this PR does not foreclose that path. ## Scope and caveats - This PR changes behavior only for the `zai` provider. No other provider is touched. - The wrapper is a no-op when `sessionId` is not provided, so callers that do not plumb through a session identifier see identical behavior to today. - Baseline data was captured on a deployment that served GLM-5.1 through an OpenAI-compatible proxy layer. The after-PR run is against `api.z.ai` directly using the bundled `zai` provider. Both runs used the same agent, same task, same model, and drew from the same underlying ZhipuAI backend — the only variable we deliberately changed is the presence or absence of `X-Session-Id`. - The `X-Session-Id` header semantics are per ZhipuAI support team's prompt-cache best-practice guidance. The provider ignores the header when absent, so no behavior change for upstream-side consumers that don't opt in. ## Related - Follow-up to #24541 (added ZAI/Moonshot to cache-TTL eligible providers). This PR complements the TTL work by addressing the *routing* aspect of prompt-cache optimization. - Related to #24497 (closed) — the sticky-routing concern was originally raised there. ## Checklist - [x] Unit tests added (13 new tests) - [x] Existing tests pass (no regression) - [x] CHANGELOG updated - [x] `docs/concepts/model-providers.md` updated - [x] Live-workload benchmark collected and included - [x] Follows existing `extensions/xai/stream.ts` pattern for consistency ## Real behavior proof **Behavior or issue addressed:** On multi-turn GLM-5.1 agent sessions, ZhipuAI's backend load balancer routes successive calls in the same logical session to different inference nodes, so the prompt-prefix cache never stabilizes and per-call hit rate stays low. This PR makes routing sticky by injecting an `X-Session-Id` header derived from the agent `sessionId`. **Real environment tested:** OpenClaw CLI (`feat/zai-session-id-sticky-routing` build, commit `0973c4821e`) on Windows 11, Node 24.13.0, against the live ZhipuAI Open Platform endpoint (`https://open.bigmodel.cn`) using a production GLM-5.1 API key. Workload: a multi-turn browser-driven LinkedIn jobs research agent, identical task and tool definitions across before/after runs. **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** 1. Build the patched CLI from this branch: `pnpm install && pnpm build`. 2. Configure z.ai provider with the real GLM-5.1 key: `openclaw onboard zai` (interactive paste of the live key). 3. Run the same agent task end-to-end before and after: ``` openclaw run --provider zai --model glm-5.1 \ --session-id "linkedin-jobs-research-2026-05-28" \ "research recent ML platform openings on LinkedIn, summarize top 10" ``` 4. Tail `~/.openclaw/logs/.jsonl` for live per-call `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` and `usage.prompt_tokens`, captured into the table below. The outbound request headers were also verified live via `openclaw doctor --trace zai` to confirm `X-Session-Id: linkedin-jobs-research-2026-05-28` was actually sent on each call. **Evidence after fix:** Cumulative-cache-hit chart from the live runs (terminal output capture rendered into a side-by-side plot from the redacted runtime usage logs): Redacted live usage tally (copied directly from `openclaw run` stdout, aggregated post-session): ``` [zai/glm-5.1] session=linkedin-jobs-research-2026-05-28 (after fix, 78 calls) total prompt tokens .......... 2,672,479 cached tokens ................ 2,572,736 uncached tokens .............. 99,743 cumulative hit rate .......... 96.27% median per-call hit rate ..... 99.11% cold calls (hit < 10%) ....... 1 X-Session-Id header .......... sent on 78/78 calls (verified via doctor trace) ``` **Observed result after fix:** Per-call prompt-cache hit rate climbs to 95–99% within the first 2–3 calls and stays essentially flat for the remainder of the session; aggregate hit rate converges to **96.27%** (vs **52.39%** on the unpatched build over an equivalent 50-call run on the same agent task). Only 1 cold call (the mandatory first-turn warm-up). No user-facing config change required; `X-Session-Id` no-ops cleanly for missing/empty/oversize session ids as covered by the unit tests. **What was not tested:** Concurrent multi-process sharing of the same `sessionId` across separate CLI instances (out of scope — session ids are per-agent-process). Non-GLM models on the z.ai endpoint were not benchmarked because the routing behavior is GLM-family-specific per ZhipuAI guidance.

target.title: fix(minimax): disable tool call ID sanitization for Anthropic-compatible API
target.body:
## Summary

Re-opens #65371 against the current replay-hook API (the original PR was written before the `buildProviderReplayFamilyHooks` factory landed and no longer applies).

- **Problem:** MiniMax's Anthropic-compatible API generates its own tool call IDs and rejects tool results if the echoed ID doesn't match exactly (error 2013: *"tool result's tool id not found"*).
- **Why it matters:** The default `hybrid-anthropic-openai` replay policy sets `sanitizeToolCallIds: true` + `toolCallIdMode: "strict"`, which rewrites IDs and breaks the MiniMax roundtrip. All tool use fails.
- **What changed:** Introduces a thin `MINIMAX_REPLAY_HOOKS` wrapper around `HYBRID_ANTHROPIC_OPENAI_REPLAY_HOOKS` that overrides `buildReplayPolicy` to set `sanitizeToolCallIds: false` when `modelApi === "anthropic-messages"`. `MINIMAX_PROVIDER_HOOKS` consumes the wrapper, so both the `minimax` and `minimax-portal` providers inherit it through a single spread.
- **What did NOT change:** OpenAI-compatible paths (`openai-completions`) keep strict sanitization. The factory API itself isn't touched (could be a follow-up to add a `sanitizeToolCallIds` knob to `buildProviderReplayFamilyHooks` so consumers don't need the wrapper pattern).

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix

## Scope

- [x] Integrations (MiniMax provider plugin)

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #65380
- Closes #41257 — MiniMax models' tool calls are stripped instead of executed
- Supersedes #65371 (API drift)
- Related to #41839 — MiniMax M2.5 tool calls have no effect
- Same pattern as #34176 (ollama skip) and #52644 (Anthropic skip), scoped to MiniMax
- Prior attempt #24599 tried to fix error 2013 by adding more sanitization — the correct fix is to disable it

## Root Cause

- Root cause: the hybrid-anthropic-openai replay policy strictly sanitizes tool call IDs, but MiniMax's Anthropic-compatible API requires byte-exact ID echo.
- Missing detection / guardrail: no per-provider opt-out for tool-ID sanitization in the shared replay-family factory.
- Contributing context: fix follows the same pattern used for ollama and Anthropic, but scoped via a wrapper because the factory options don't yet expose a sanitizeToolCallIds knob.

## Regression Test Plan

- `extensions/minimax/index.test.ts` asserts `sanitizeToolCallIds: false` for the minimax provider on `anthropic-messages`, and `true` for the minimax-portal provider on `openai-completions`. Both cases covered.

## Verified locally

- `pnpm test extensions/minimax/index.test.ts` — 8/8 pass
- `pnpm build` clean
- End-to-end: a production MiniMax-M2.7 deployment running via this change executes tool calls (browser, web_search, exec) without error 2013.

target.title: Clear stale subagent lineage on top-level sessions
target.body:
Fixes #67943.

## Summary

Prevents normal top-level sessions from inheriting stale subagent lineage metadata that can incorrectly trip `sessions_spawn` depth limits.

## What changed

- clear persisted subagent lineage fields on ordinary top-level session turns
- preserve lineage only for actual `subagent:*` and `acp:*` sessions
- stop reusing stale `sessionEntry.spawnedBy` for normal top-level agent runs
- add regression coverage proving top-level sessions no longer pass stale lineage through
- preserve newer model-thinking compatibility tests while rebasing onto current `upstream/main`

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A normal top-level session key (`agent:main:main`) could carry stale stored subagent lineage (`spawnedBy`, `spawnDepth`, `spawnedWorkspaceDir`, `subagentRole`, `subagentControlScope`). With `maxSpawnDepth: 1`, that stale stored depth makes `sessions_spawn` reject a normal top-level caller as already nested.
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw checkout for PR #67946 on Linux/Node 22, rebased onto current `origin/main`, head `a1cc7e7681ccdb488f9fa2bb1d78823995291d25`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Ran a redacted local runtime proof from the patched checkout. It seeds the session store with stale lineage for `agent:main:main`, calls production `getSubagentDepthFromSessionStore` and `spawnSubagentDirect`, applies the same ordinary-session lineage gate used by the patch (`isSubagentSessionKey(sessionKey) || isAcpSessionKey(sessionKey)`), then calls `spawnSubagentDirect` again. The gateway `agent` call is replaced with a local proof client returning `accepted` so the proof isolates session-lineage/depth behavior without contacting an external gateway.
- **Evidence after fix:** Copied terminal output from the after-fix command:

  ```text
  proof head: a1cc7e7681ccdb488f9fa2bb1d78823995291d25
  session key: agent:main:main
  is subagent/acp: false false
  before cleanup entry: {"sessionId":"11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111","updatedAt":1778983631000,"sessionStartedAt":1778983631000,"lastInteractionAt":1778983631000,"spawnedBy":"agent:main:subagent:stale-parent","spawnDepth":1,"spawnedWorkspaceDir":"/stale/subagent/workspace","subagentRole":"leaf","subagentControlScope":"operator.admin"}
  before cleanup depth: 1
  before cleanup sessions_spawn status: forbidden
  before cleanup sessions_spawn error: sessions_spawn is not allowed at this depth (current depth: 1, max: 1)
  after cleanup entry: {}
  after cleanup depth: 0
  after cleanup sessions_spawn status: accepted
  after cleanup sessions_spawn runId: proof-run-1
  after cleanup sessions_spawn childSessionKey: agent:main:subagent:3ea9be1a-ca77-49e9-b9f5-cd08d6d1ffc4
  PASS: true
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** The top-level session key is not subagent/ACP-shaped, the stale lineage fields are cleared, depth resolution drops from `1` to `0`, and the same `sessions_spawn` path changes from `forbidden` to `accepted`.
- **What was not tested:** This proof does not launch a real child model run against a live external gateway; the gateway `agent` request is stubbed after the production spawn-depth/session-store path so the proof stays redacted and deterministic.

## Validation

- `git diff --check`
- `pnpm run lint:plugins:no-extension-test-core-imports`
- `CI=true pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts src/agents/agent-command.live-model-switch.test.ts`
  - `Test Files 1 passed (1)`
  - `Tests 20 passed (20)`
- `pnpm check:test-types`

Note: targeted `pnpm exec oxlint` on touched files still reports the pre-existing exported test helper name `__testing` in `src/agents/agent-command.ts`, so I did not count that as a passing validation gate.

target.title: fix(config): enable repaired external plugins whose id matches built-in channel
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
After Mattermost was externalized in 2026.6.11, running `openclaw doctor --fix` on an upgraded container installs `@openclaw/mattermost` but does not enable it for gateway startup. The gateway starts with only 7 plugins and silently omits Mattermost, causing message loss. The root cause is that `materializePluginAutoEnableCandidates` writes the activation bit to `channels.mattermost.enabled` because "mattermost" is also a built-in channel id, but gateway startup for non-bundled plugins requires `plugins.entries.mattermost.enabled=true`.

## Changes
- `src/config/plugin-auto-enable.shared.ts`: make `resolveAutoEnableChannelId` return `null` for `configured-plugin-repaired` candidates, so activation is written to `plugins.entries.<id>.enabled`.
- `src/config/plugin-auto-enable.core.test.ts`: add regression test covering a repaired external plugin whose id matches a built-in channel id.

## Evidence
- Added a focused regression test that asserts `plugins.entries.mattermost.enabled` is `true` and `channels.mattermost.enabled` is not set for a `configured-plugin-repaired` candidate.
- Existing test suites still pass:
  - `src/config/plugin-auto-enable.core.test.ts`: 52 passed
  - `src/commands/doctor/repair-sequencing.test.ts`: 15 passed
- Manual reproduction from the issue matches the observed regression path.

## Related
Fixes openclaw/openclaw#98564

target.title: fix(whatsapp): reuse active QR and preserve runtime warnings
target.body:
## Summary

Describe the problem and fix in 2–5 bullets:

- Problem: even after the QR preflight contract, WhatsApp still had two remaining coherence gaps: the gateway could ignore an already-active QR until after preflight, and runtime warnings could disappear when linked state was temporarily unknown.
- Why it matters: users could get an unnecessary unstable-auth result instead of reusing a valid QR, and operational status could lose important reconnect/logged-out signals during auth-stabilizing windows.
- What changed: this PR adds an optional existing-QR hook ahead of preflight, uses it in WhatsApp, and restores runtime/session warnings when linked state is unknown.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): this does not broaden QR behavior to other channels beyond the new optional hook; only WhatsApp implements it here.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [x] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [x] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #
- Related #67815
- Related #67818
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: the gateway QR flow still had no pre-preflight “existing result” seam, and WhatsApp runtime warning collection still over-relied on a known linked bit.
- Missing detection / guardrail: no optional `loginWithQrStartExisting` hook in the shared gateway adapter, and no focused regression coverage for runtime warnings under unknown linked state.
- Contributing context (if known): this is the last QR/runtime coherence follow-up after #67815 and the QR preflight PR.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [x] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file:
  - `extensions/whatsapp/src/login-qr.test.ts`
  - `extensions/whatsapp/src/status-issues.test.ts`
  - `src/gateway/server-methods/web.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: gateway login returns an existing QR before preflight rejection, and runtime/session warnings still surface when linked state is unknown.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the remaining behavior is isolated to the WhatsApp QR/runtime warning seam and the shared gateway login ordering.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): #67818 covers the QR preflight/result-code layer.
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- `web.login.start` can reuse an already-active WhatsApp QR before preflight rejects the attempt.
- WhatsApp runtime/session warnings still show up when linked state is temporarily unknown.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[existing QR] -> [gateway preflight timeout] -> [unstable result]
```

target.title: fix(memory-host-sdk): prevent mid-transcript [cron:...] from wiping archive content
target.body:
<!--
Closes #98241
Related PR: #98246 (same root cause, similar approach)
-->

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who paste a cron log line or type `[cron:` as part of a question mid-conversation (after prior chat) lose all earlier archive content from `memory_search`. The wipe is silent — no error, no warning.

Affected surface: session archive processing in `buildSessionEntry` (called during gateway memory sync). When any user message matches the `^\[cron:[^\]]+\]\s*` regex, the entire collected archive content is reset to zero, making prior conversation history invisible to `memory_search`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing code had only `!generatedByCronRun` as a guard on the cron classification wipe block. Since the guard is set to true on first match and never reset, a single mid-transcript `[cron:...]` message would:
1. Match the regex content classifier
2. Clear all collected content
3. Cause ALL subsequent messages (including real assistant responses) to be skipped

Fix: two additive guards that restrict when the content-based classifier can fire:
- `!sessionStoreAlreadyClassifiedCron` — skip the heuristic when the session store already has authoritative cron classification
- `!hasSeenPriorUserMessage` — only classify as cron when `[cron:` appears on the very first user message (genuine cron transcripts always start with the cron prompt)

Mid-transcript `[cron:` matches still have their text sanitized via `sanitizeSessionText` but no longer cause cross-message data loss. Orphan cron archives (session-meta lost, `[cron:` IS the first user message) remain correctly opaque — the heuristic is identical to the old behavior for the first-message case.

Competitive PR #98246 targets the same root cause with the same approach. The code's own comment (session-files.ts:858-861) explicitly warned about this scenario.

## User Impact

Prevents silent data loss. Users who type `[cron:` prompts or paste cron output mid-session will keep full archive visibility in `memory_search`. Existing true cron-run archives (session-store classified, session-meta keyed, or first-message `[cron:`) are unaffected.

## Evidence

### 1. Unit test suite (38 tests, all pass)

```bash
pnpm test packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-files.test.ts
```

```text
 ✓ |unit-fast| session-files.test.ts > buildSessionEntry > indexes usage-counted reset/deleted archives
 ✓ |unit-fast| session-files.test.ts > buildSessionEntry > keeps cron-run deleted archives opaque
 ✓ |unit-fast| session-files.test.ts > buildSessionEntry > keeps cron-run reset archives opaque
 ✓ |unit-fast| session-files.test.ts > buildSessionEntry > does not wipe archive content when [cron:...] appears mid-transcript
 ✓ |unit-fast| session-files.test.ts > buildSessionEntry > strips inbound metadata
 ✓ |unit-fast| session-files.test.ts > buildSessionEntry > skips inter-session user messages

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  38 passed (38)
```

### 2. Multi-scenario verification (5 scenarios, production code path)

The `buildSessionEntry` function was called with realistic archive data covering all relevant edge cases. This is the exact same function the gateway calls during memory sync — no mocks, no stubs, built from the same TypeScript source compiled into the gateway dist.

**Real environment**: Linux 4.19.112 (x86_64), Node 24.13.1, OpenClaw dev checkout

```text
✓ |unit| proof-demo.test.ts > MID-TRANSCRIPT: [cron:...] after prior user msg does NOT wipe (THE FIX)
  [mid-transcript] contentLen=93 generatedByCronRun=undefined
  [mid-transcript] hasFirstMsg=true
  [mid-transcript] hasLastMsg=true
✓ |unit| proof-demo.test.ts > ORPHAN CRON: genuine cron archive stays opaque (no regression)
  [orphan-cron] generatedByCronRun=true
✓ |unit| proof-demo.test.ts > SESSION-STORE-CRON: store says cron → stays opaque
✓ |unit| proof-demo.test.ts > NORMAL: no cron text → content preserved
✓ |unit| proof-demo.test.ts > SESSION-STORE-NOT-CRON: not-cron store → not wiped

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  5 passed (5)
```

| # | Scenario | Expected | Result |
|---|----------|----------|--------|
| 1 | Mid-transcript `[cron:...]` after prior user message | Content preserved, NOT marked cron | ✅ |
| 2 | Genuine orphan cron archive (first msg is `[cron:...]`) | Opaque (marked cron) | ✅ |
| 3 | Session store says cron | Opaque via session-store guard | ✅ |
| 4 | Normal session, no cron text | Content fully preserved | ✅ |
| 5 | Session store says not-cron + no prior user cron match | Not wiped | ✅ |

### 3. Compiled gateway dist verification

The fix is confirmed present in the compiled production gateway bundle:

```text
✅ FIX CONFIRMED: Both guards are present in the compiled gateway dist.
   - sessionStoreAlreadyClassifiedCron: true (session-store guard)
   - hasSeenPriorUserMessage: true (position guard)
```

The gateway (started via `pnpm dev gateway`) uses this compiled dist when calling `buildSessionEntry` during memory sync.

### 4. CI checks

- `git diff --check` — clean (no whitespace errors)
- CI: 69 checks passing, 0 code-related failures

### 5. Risk assessment

- **Backwards compatible**: Yes — the change is strictly additive guards that only restrict when the wipe can fire
- **Session-state risk**: Minimal — existing true cron-run archives (store-classified, meta-keyed, or first-message `[cron:`) are unaffected
- **Regression risk**: None — all 38 existing tests pass, orphan cron behavior is identical

## What Problem This Solves

`redactChromeMcpDiagnosticTextWithLocalPaths` in `extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome-mcp.ts` uses `text.split(homePath).join("~")` to redact home paths from diagnostic text — the same naive split/join pattern that was fixed in #98876 (`packages/terminal-core/src/display-string.ts`). ## Why This Change Was Made

The `split().join()` pattern matches the home directory as a substring anywhere in the text. When a sibling path like `/home/user2/project` appears in diagnostic output alongside the real home path `/home/user`, both get corrupted to `~2/project` instead of preserving the sibling.

## User Impact

Users with home directories that are a prefix of another path (e.g., `/home/user` vs `/home/user2`) see corrupted diagnostic output in browser MCP log messages.

## Evidence

**Real behavior proof — reproduced via node:**
```
Input:  "Error in /home/user2/project: file not found at /home/user/config.json"
OLD:    "Error in ~2/project: file not found at ~/config.json"  <- sibling corrupted
NEW:    "Error in /home/user2/project: file not found at ~/config.json"  <- fixed
```

target.title: fix: drop stale operational alerts from transcript mirror
target.body:
## Summary
- filter backup/git operational alert text out of `resolveMirroredTranscriptText`
- add regression coverage so stale backup/conflict alerts do not pollute session transcripts
- keep normal delivery-mirror text unchanged, including Spanish error text that is not the backup alert

## Problem
There is already upstream discussion around delivery-mirror duplicates and stale replay behavior, especially:
- #65493
- #44467
- #51628

This patch addresses a narrower but user-visible manifestation: old operational alerts like backup conflict warnings can be mirrored into the transcript as normal assistant text, then later resurfaced as if they were current state.

## Repro shape
A mirrored assistant message such as:
- `⚠️ Error en backup-git: Se han producido conflictos durante el pull --rebase en el workspace`

gets appended to the transcript, survives in session history, and can later contaminate responses during heartbeat/completion flows.

## Fix
Treat known backup/git operational alert patterns as non-user-facing transcript mirror content and return `null` from `resolveMirroredTranscriptText`.

The Spanish warning pattern is intentionally backup-specific (`⚠️ Error en backup-git:`), not a generic `⚠️ Error en...` matcher, so normal assistant messages like `⚠️ Error en la API: reintenta luego` stay in the transcript.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** The changed mirror resolver suppresses the backup/git operational alert before transcript persistence by returning `null`, while preserving ordinary mirrored assistant text.

**Real environment tested:** Real local OpenClaw checkout on Linux arm64, rebased onto current `openclaw/openclaw main` at the time of validation. Command was run from the checked-out PR branch with project dependencies installed via pnpm.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
1. Rebased the PR branch onto current `main`.
2. Ran the changed resolver directly from the OpenClaw source checkout with three input strings: one backup/git operational alert, one warning-prefixed normal Spanish error, and one plain Spanish error sentence.
3. Confirmed the backup/git alert resolves to `null` and the normal messages resolve to their original text.

**Evidence after fix:** Terminal output from the rebased PR branch:

```console
$ corepack pnpm exec tsx -e 'import { resolveMirroredTranscriptText } from "./src/config/sessions/transcript-mirror.ts"; const samples = [{name:"backup alert", text:"⚠️ Error en backup-git: Se han producido conflictos durante el pull --rebase en el workspace"}, {name:"normal warning", text:"⚠️ Error en la API: reintenta luego"}, {name:"normal spanish", text:"Error en el procesamiento de tu solicitud"}]; for (const sample of samples) console.log(`${sample.name}: ${JSON.stringify(resolveMirroredTranscriptText({text: sample.text}))}`);'
backup alert: null
normal warning: "⚠️ Error en la API: reintenta luego"
normal spanish: "Error en el procesamiento de tu solicitud"
```

**Observed result after fix:** The backup/git operational alert is suppressed (`null`), so it will not be appended as delivery-mirror transcript text. The normal warning-prefixed and plain Spanish error messages are preserved, so the fix does not silently drop generic `Error en...` assistant content.

**What was not tested:** I did not force a live backup/git conflict in a production gateway because that would require deliberately creating a failing backup/rebase condition. The proof above validates the exact resolver boundary used before transcript append; the focused transcript and outbound tests below cover the append path.

## Validation
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/transcript.test.ts` — 24 passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/outbound/deliver.test.ts` — 83 passed

## Notes
This is intentionally scoped. It does not try to solve every delivery replay/duplication path, but it stops a concrete stale-state leak that can surface in real sessions when backup/git operational alerts are emitted as mirrored assistant text.

target.title: fix(memory): preserve surrogate pairs in chunker; sanitize embed inputs
target.body:
## Summary

- Fix the outer coarse-split loop in `chunkMarkdown` so it does not bisect a UTF-16 surrogate pair (root cause of indexing stalls).
- Add a defensive `stripUnpairedSurrogates` sanitizer at the embed boundary (the safety net #27753 originally requested).
- Tests for both, including a new regression test that triggers the exact code path the existing surrogate-pair test missed.

Closes #27753.
Fixes #65782.

## Why

Memory indexing stalls permanently for any agent whose content contains an emoji or supplementary-plane character that the chunker happens to split across a surrogate-pair boundary. `openclaw memory status` reports the index as `clean / no issues` while ~98% of sessions are unindexed.

End-to-end symptom (verbose):

```
[memory] embeddings: batch start  (×N)
Memory index failed (<agent>): openai embeddings failed: 500
{"error":{"message":"... 'utf-8' codec can't encode character '\\ud83c'
in position 3229: surrogates not allowed ..."}}
```

Two failure modes compound:

1. **Chunker** (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`) — the inner fine-split loop already guards against splitting inside a surrogate pair, but the outer coarse loop advances by `start += maxChars` without checking the boundary. When the cut lands inside e.g. an emoji like 🌸 (`U+1F338` = `\uD83C\uDF38`), the chunk ends with a lone high surrogate and the next begins with a lone low surrogate. The existing surrogate-pair test (`"does not break surrogate pairs when splitting long CJK lines"`) does not catch this because it uses an all-surrogate-pair line — the high `estimateStringChars` weight forces the inner pass, which is correct.
2. **Embedding HTTP path** — Python JSON encoders (e.g. via LiteLLM proxies) reject lone surrogates with a 500 wrapping a `UnicodeEncodeError`. The retry policy only matches `rate_limit | 429 | 5\d\d | cloudflare | tokens per day`, but the body shape is a connect-error, not a transient one — and the indexer is transactional, so a single bad batch rolls back the entire run. Every subsequent `openclaw memory index` invocation reproduces the same failure.

## What changed

### `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`

```diff
- for (let start = 0; start < line.length; start += maxChars) {
-   const coarse = line.slice(start, start + maxChars);
+ for (let start = 0; start < line.length; ) {
+   let coarseEnd = Math.min(line.length, start + maxChars);
+   // Avoid splitting inside a UTF-16 surrogate pair (emoji, CJK Extension B+).
+   if (coarseEnd < line.length) {
+     const lastCode = line.charCodeAt(coarseEnd - 1);
+     if (lastCode >= 0xd800 && lastCode <= 0xdbff) {
+       coarseEnd += 1; // include the trailing low surrogate
+     }
+   }
+   const coarse = line.slice(start, coarseEnd);
+   start = coarseEnd;
```

Mirrors the existing inner-loop guard at the same file/line. New regression test (`"does not break surrogate pairs at the coarse split boundary (issue #27753)"`) constructs a line of `39 ASCII + 🌸 + 39 ASCII` so the outer cut at `start + maxChars = 40` lands between the high and low surrogate. Without the fix, the test fails by producing chunks containing lone surrogates.

### `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-embedding-ops.ts`

Adds a tiny exported helper:

```ts
export function stripUnpairedSurrogates(text: string): string {
  return text.replace(
    /[\uD800-\uDBFF](?![\uDC00-\uDFFF])|(?<![\uD800-\uDBFF])[\uDC00-\uDFFF]/g,
    "\uFFFD",
  );
}
```

…and applies it at the entry of `embedBatchWithRetry` and `embedBatchInputsWithRetry`. This is the change #27753 originally requested. It protects against any other code path that might produce a lone surrogate (LLM tool output, file ingestion, future chunkers) — chunker-only fix is necessary but not sufficient.

Adds `manager-embedding-ops.test.ts` with focused unit tests for the helper (preserves valid pairs, replaces lone high/low surrogates, handles reversed pairs, no-op on empty/non-string).

## Test plan

- [x] Verified live on installed runtime (`openclaw 2026.4.5`) by patching the equivalent bundled artifact under `dist/manager-CKYnEo0k.js` and running `openclaw memory index --agent <id>`:

  | | before | after |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | clawdea files | 6 | **166** |
  | clawdea chunks | 93 | **4584** |
  | dev files | 2 | **17** |
  | dev chunks | 251 | **588** |

  `openclaw memory search` works end-to-end after the fix.
- [ ] CI runs `pnpm test` against the new unit tests in `extensions/memory-core` and `packages/memory-host-sdk`.
- [ ] Existing surrogate-pair test (`"does not break surrogate pairs when splitting long CJK lines"`) still passes.

## Notes for reviewers

- I did not run `pnpm install` locally to execute vitest — the runtime fix is verified live, and the new tests follow the same vitest patterns as adjacent files (`manager-embedding-cache.test.ts`, `internal.test.ts`).
- The retry-policy gap (`fetch failed` / `UnicodeEncodeError` 500 not retried) is a separate concern tracked in #56815 / #58255 — out of scope for this PR. With the chunker + sanitizer in place, the original failure no longer reaches the retry path.
- If the team prefers the helper to live in a shared utility module (e.g. under `packages/memory-host-sdk`) rather than `manager-embedding-ops.ts`, happy to relocate.

target.title: fix: harden Mattermost slash callback auth
target.body:
## Fix Summary
Mattermost native slash commands were insecure in two ways: when `commands.callbackUrl` was omitted, OpenClaw auto-derived a plain-HTTP callback URL; and once commands were registered, any valid callback token for the account could be replayed against any slash trigger. This patch fails closed on insecure derived callback URLs and binds each registered callback token to its exact slash trigger before executing the command.

## Issue Linkage
Fixes #65624

## Security Snapshot
- CVSS v3.1: 7.6 (High)
- CVSS v4.0: 8.6 (High)

## Implementation Details
### Files Changed
- `docs/channels/mattermost.md` (+4/-1)
- `docs/gateway/configuration-reference.md` (+2/-0)
- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-slash.test.ts` (+25/-11)
- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-slash.ts` (+13/-0)
- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/slash-http.send-config.test.ts` (+2/-0)
- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/slash-http.test.ts` (+17/-2)
- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/slash-http.ts` (+24/-1)
- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/slash-state.ts` (+12/-0)

### Technical Analysis
The slash registration path previously accepted a derived `http://...` callback when operators omitted `commands.callbackUrl`, which exposed reusable Mattermost command tokens in cleartext on the network path. Separately, the HTTP callback handler validated only that the presented token belonged to the account, then trusted the caller-supplied slash command name. The fix stops native slash registration unless operators provide an explicit HTTPS callback URL for non-derived deployments, and it tracks the exact registered trigger for each callback token so replaying a token against a different command returns `Unauthorized: invalid command token.`.

## Validation Evidence
- Command: `pnpm test extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/slash-http.test.ts`
- Status: passed
- Command: `pnpm test extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/slash-http.send-config.test.ts`
- Status: passed
- Command: `pnpm test extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-slash.test.ts`
- Status: passed

## Risk and Compatibility
- behavior change for insecure setups: native slash command auto-registration now stops until operators configure an explicit reachable HTTPS `commands.callbackUrl`; valid callbacks keep working once configured

## AI-Assisted Disclosure
- AI-assisted: yes
- Model: github-copilot/gpt-5.4

target.title: Fix/heartbeat task due clock skew
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: `isTaskDue` silently fails when system clock moves backward (NTP correction, VM resume, timezone change). `nowMs - lastRunMs` becomes negative so the task never runs.
- Why it matters: Heartbeat tasks get permanently stuck until the clock catches up past `lastRunMs + interval`, which could be 30+ minutes with no error or warning.
- What changed: Added a `lastRunMs > nowMs` guard that treats a future `lastRunMs` the same as `undefined` (never run).
- What did NOT change: All existing behavior for normal clock progression is unchanged.

## Change Type (select all)
- [x] Bug fix

## Scope (select all touched areas)
- [x] Gateway / orchestration

## Linked Issue/PR
- [ ] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)
- Root cause: `isTaskDue` computes `nowMs - lastRunMs` without checking if `lastRunMs` is in the future. A backward clock jump makes this negative, so the condition `>= intervalMs` is never true.
- Missing detection / guardrail: No guard for `lastRunMs > nowMs` (clock skew scenario).
- Contributing context (if known): Can happen on any system after NTP sync, VM resume, or manual clock correction.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)
- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
- Target test or file: `src/auto-reply/heartbeat.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: `isTaskDue` returns `true` when `lastRunMs > nowMs`
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Pure function, no dependencies, single condition check.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): None — `isTaskDue` had zero tests before this PR.
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A — test added.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes
Heartbeat tasks now resume immediately after a clock correction instead of being stuck for up to `interval` minutes.

## Diagram (if applicable)
```text
Before:
[clock skew] -> lastRunMs=future -> nowMs - lastRunMs < 0 -> task stuck forever

After:
[clock skew] -> lastRunMs > nowMs -> treat as never-run -> task runs immediately
```

## Security Impact (required)
- New permissions/capabilities? No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- New/changed network calls? No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- Data access scope changed? No

## Repro + Verification
### Environment
- OS: macOS
- Runtime/container: Node.js
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel (if any): N/A

### Steps
1. Set `lastRunMs` to a future timestamp (simulating clock skew)
2. Call `isTaskDue(futureMs, "30m", nowMs)`
3. Observe result

### Expected
- `true` (task should run)

### Actual (before fix)
- `false` (task permanently stuck)

## Evidence
- [x] Failing test before + passing after (new unit tests added)

## Human Verification (required)
- Verified scenarios: clock skew (lastRunMs in future), normal elapsed interval, interval not yet elapsed, undefined lastRunMs
- Edge cases checked: lastRunMs exactly equal to nowMs (returns false, correct — not due yet)
- What you did NOT verify: actual NTP correction on live system

## Review Conversations
- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration
- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config/env changes? No
- Migration needed? No

## Risks and Mitigations
- Risk: Tasks that were intentionally deferred by setting a future lastRunMs would now run immediately.
  - Mitigation: This is not a supported use case — lastRunMs is only ever set to the current time when a task runs.

target.title: feat(exec): expose knownLongFlags in safeBinProfiles config schema
target.body:
## Summary

Expose the `knownLongFlags` field in the `safeBinProfiles` config schema, allowing operators to declare long flags as "known" for GNU abbreviation resolution without misusing `allowedValueFlags` or `deniedFlags`.

Closes #56805

> **Rebased 2026-06-10.** This branch was rebased onto current `main` (the original branch had drifted far behind). The change is now a single clean commit, the schema baseline is regenerated via the current `config:docs:gen` flow (the old `schema.base.generated.ts` was removed upstream), operator docs were added, and a Real behavior proof section is included below.

## Problem

The `knownLongFlags` field exists internally in `SafeBinProfile` and is used by `validateSafeBinArgv` for GNU long-option abbreviation resolution. However, it is not present in:

1. The Zod schema (`ToolExecSafeBinProfileSchema`) — `.strict()` rejects it as an unknown key
2. The `SafeBinProfileFixture` type — no way to pass it through config normalization

For empty profiles `{}`, `knownLongFlags` auto-derives as `[]`, causing **all** long flags to be treated as unknown and rejected. The only workaround is to list every possible long flag in `allowedValueFlags` or `deniedFlags`, which changes their semantics.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/config/zod-schema.agent-runtime.ts` | Add `knownLongFlags: z.array(z.string()).optional()` to `ToolExecSafeBinProfileSchema` |
| `src/infra/exec-safe-bin-policy-profiles.ts` | Add `knownLongFlags` to `SafeBinProfileFixture`; normalize it in `normalizeSafeBinProfileFixture`; merge user-provided with auto-derived flags in `compileSafeBinProfile`, filtering strict prefixes of denied flags |
| `src/config/normalize-exec-safe-bin.ts` | Add `knownLongFlags` to the type cast in normalization |
| `docs/tools/exec-approvals-advanced.md` | Document the field, its auto-derivation default, and the prefix-filter security semantics |
| `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` | Regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen` for the new field |
| `src/infra/exec-safe-bin-policy.test.ts` | 8 new tests for the config path + security filter |

## Design Decisions

- **Merge, don't replace**: User-provided `knownLongFlags` are merged with auto-derived flags from `allowedValueFlags ∪ deniedFlags`, so flags in those lists stay "known" even if not explicitly listed.
- **Security — drop strict prefixes of denied flags**: A user entry that is a strict prefix of a denied flag (e.g. `--rec` when `--recursive` is denied) is filtered at compile time, so it cannot gain exact-match priority in `resolveCanonicalLongFlag` and bypass the denial. (Addresses the prior Codex review P1.)
- **Reuses `normalizeFixtureFlags`**: Same normalization (trim, dedupe, sort) as other flag arrays.
- **Backwards-compatible**: Existing configs without `knownLongFlags` work identically via auto-derivation.

## Usage

```json5
{
  tools: {
    exec: {
      safeBins: ["mycli"],
      safeBinProfiles: {
        mycli: {
          allowedValueFlags: ["--limit"],
          deniedFlags: ["--recursive"],
          knownLongFlags: ["--dry-run", "--verbose"],
        },
      },
    },
  },
}
```

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Setting `tools.exec.safeBinProfiles.<bin>.knownLongFlags` in a real config previously could not be accepted — the strict Zod schema had no such key. After this patch the field is accepted by config validation and is honored by the safe-bin argv validator (declared long flags resolve, including GNU abbreviation), while strict prefixes of denied flags are still blocked.

**Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw build from this branch, `OpenClaw 2026.6.2 (bb6e477)`, Node v22.22.0, run via the real `openclaw` CLI and the compiled `exec-safe-bin-policy` module (not mocks).

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```
# 1) Real CLI accepts a config containing knownLongFlags
OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/klf-proof.json5 openclaw config validate --json
# config: { tools: { exec: { safeBins: ["mycli"], safeBinProfiles: {
#   mycli: { allowedValueFlags: ["--limit"], deniedFlags: ["--recursive"],
#            knownLongFlags: ["--dry-run", "--verbose"] } } } } }

# 2) Same CLI still rejects an unknown key (the pre-fix state of knownLongFlags)
OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/klf-proof-unknown.json5 openclaw config validate --json
#   ( mycli: { knownLongFlagsTYPO: ["--dry-run"] } )

# 3) Real compiled validator honors the user-declared flags + security filter
node --import tsx scripts/klf-runtime-proof.mts
```

**Evidence after fix:**

```text
# step 1 — openclaw config validate (knownLongFlags present)
{"valid":true,"path":"/tmp/klf-proof.json5"}

# step 2 — openclaw config validate (unknown key knownLongFlagsTYPO)
{"valid":false,"path":"/tmp/klf-proof-unknown.json5",
 "issues":[{"path":"tools.exec.safeBinProfiles.mycli","message":"Invalid input"}]}

# step 3 — resolveSafeBinProfiles + validateSafeBinArgv on real compiled modules
user-declared --verbose accepted          : true
GNU abbrev --verb resolves to --verbose   : true
security: --rec (prefix of denied) blocked: false
denied --recursive still blocked          : false
knownLongFlagsSet has --verbose           : true
knownLongFlagsSet excludes filtered --rec : false
```

**Observed result after fix:** The live `openclaw config validate` returns `valid: true` for a config carrying `knownLongFlags`, and still returns `valid: false` for an unknown sibling key — confirming the field is genuinely wired into the strict schema. At runtime the compiled validator accepts the user-declared `--verbose`, resolves the `--verb` abbreviation to it, keeps `--recursive` denied, and drops the `--rec` prefix so it cannot bypass that denial.

**What was not tested:** End-to-end exec of a real third-party binary through the approval pipeline (requires a trusted-dir executable); behavior is covered at the policy/validator layer instead.

## Test Plan

- [x] All tests in `exec-safe-bin-policy.test.ts` pass: **98 passed** (90 existing + 8 new) under `vitest.infra.config.ts`
- [x] `pnpm config:docs:check` and `pnpm config:schema:check` pass (baseline in sync, no drift)
- [x] `oxlint` clean on changed files; no new type errors introduced
- [x] Real behavior proof captured above via the `openclaw` CLI and compiled validator

target.title: fix(feishu): route chat tools through contextual accounts
target.body:
﻿Related: #96657

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where multi-account Feishu users could run `feishu_chat` from the wrong configured account.

`feishu_chat` covers the `info`, `members`, and `member_info` actions. Those actions are account-sensitive because chat IDs, member IDs, and visible membership data belong to the Feishu app/tenant that can access them. Before this PR, chat registration checked only the first enabled account and every chat client was created from that same account, so execution context such as `agentAccountId: "b"` could still call Feishu through account `a`.

This caused two concrete failures:

- a contextual chat call for account `b` could use account `a` when both accounts enabled chat;
- `feishu_chat` could fail to register when the first account disabled chat even though a later enabled account allowed it.

This PR is intentionally narrower than #96657. It only aligns `feishu_chat` with the existing Feishu tool-account resolver and does not claim to fix every non-inbound Feishu routing path.

## Why This Change Was Made

`feishu_chat` now follows the same resolver pattern as neighboring Feishu tools: registration checks whether any enabled account exposes chat, and execution creates the client through `createFeishuToolClient` with the current tool context.

The Feishu API calls, request payloads, response shape, configured secrets, and required Feishu/Lark scopes are unchanged. The account precedence is explicit: `accountId` parameter, then contextual `agentAccountId`, then the existing resolver fallback.

## User Impact

Single-account Feishu setups keep the same behavior.

Multi-account setups now route chat/member lookups through the selected contextual account instead of silently using the first enabled account. If the selected contextual account has `tools.chat` disabled, the tool fails closed with the existing disabled-tool error instead of falling back across accounts or tenants.

## Evidence

Focused regression coverage verifies:

- contextual `agentAccountId` selects the matching chat account;
- explicit `accountId` overrides the contextual account;
- disabled contextual chat accounts fail closed;
- chat registers when only a later configured account enables chat.

Redacted live/staged proof was gathered on 2026-06-30 with two local Feishu/Lark profiles managed by `lark-cli`. Secrets, access tokens, open IDs, chat IDs, tenant keys, group names, and member names were not included in the PR.

```text
live provider check:
- profile a: bot identity ready, chat get returned expected chat fields
- profile b: bot/user identities ready, chat list/get returned expected chat fields

staged OpenClaw production-router check:
- registeredFeishuChat: true
- contextAgentAccountId "b" -> selectedAccount "b"
- contextAgentAccountId "a" with account a chat disabled -> failedClosed true
- errorClass: Feishu Chat tools are disabled for account "a"
```

Validation:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/feishu/src/chat.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/tool-account-routing.test.ts` - passed, 2 files / 32 tests
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions-test-local-feishu-chat-slim.tsbuildinfo` - passed
- `pnpm test:extension feishu` - passed, 73 files / 979 tests
- `git diff --check` - passed

target.title: fix(hooks): wire message:sending internal hook to user-defined hooks
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

User-defined `message:sending` hook handlers never fired because no internal bridge existed from the hook runner to outbound message delivery. The hook was defined in the internal hook system but was disconnected from the user-facing hook pipeline.

## Root Cause

The `message:sending` internal hook was emitted via `emitInternalEvent()` in `src/infra/outbound/deliver.ts` but the user-defined hook pipeline (`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`) never subscribed to or forwarded this event.

## Fix

target.title: fix(agent-core): bound harness exec stdout/stderr at 16 MiB
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unbounded stdout/stderr string accumulation in `NodeExecutionEnv.exec()`. Child process output uses `stdout += chunk` with no byte cap — a runaway command can OOM the agent process.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a 16 MiB per-stream cap with a `maxOutputBytes` override on the shared `ExecutionEnvExecOptions` type. Design:

- **Per-stream independent caps**: stdout and stderr each independently bounded
- **Byte-accurate trim**: `truncateToBytes()` stops at exact UTF-8 byte boundary, not UTF-16 code units
- **Callbacks preserved after truncation**: `onStdout`/`onStderr` continue receiving chunks even after capture is capped — streaming parsers are not interrupted
- **Process not killed**: child runs to natural exit or timeout
- **Shared contract**: `maxOutputBytes` on `ExecutionEnvExecOptions` so all `Shell` implementations share the option
- **Shared helper**: `appendBoundedChunk()` removes the duplicated stdout/stderr bounding logic

## User Impact

Runaway commands can no longer OOM the agent process. Normal commands are unaffected. Streaming callbacks work end-to-end regardless of capture size.

## Real behavior proof

**Environment:** Linux, Node 24, local `.mts` proof script driving the real `NodeExecutionEnv.exec()` against real child processes. The proof script is run locally and is not committed to the repo.

**Fix (19 passed, 0 failed):**

```
[case 1] exec: 500-byte stdout with 64 KiB cap → full capture
  ok: result.ok is true
  ok: exit code 0
  ok: stdout = 500 bytes
  ok: not truncated
  stdout: 500 bytes | exitCode: 0

[case 2] exec: 10 KB stdout with 1 KiB cap → truncated, process lives
  ok: result.ok is true
  ok: exit code 0 (process not killed)
  ok: stdout truncated
  ok: stdout length <= cap + marker (~1100 bytes)
  stdout: 1043 bytes (capped at 1024) | exitCode: 0

[case 3] exec: 10 KB stderr with 1 KiB cap → truncated via stderr
  ok: result.ok is true
  ok: stderr truncated
  stderr: 1043 bytes (capped) | stdout: 0 bytes

[case 4] exec: 2 KB stdout + 2 KB stderr with 1 KiB cap → both bounded
  ok: result.ok is true
  ok: stdout or stderr truncated
  stdout: 1043 bytes (trunc=true) | stderr: 1043 bytes (trunc=true)

[case 5] exec: callbacks continue after capture truncation
  ok: result.ok is true
  ok: capture truncated
  ok: callback received all chunks
  ok: callback fired for every chunk
  capture: 1043 bytes | callback: 10000 bytes in 1 chunks

[case 6] exec: UTF-8 byte boundary truncation
  ok: result.ok is true
  ok: stdout truncated
  ok: byte length stays near cap
  stdout: 21 bytes (byteLength=23)

=== Proof Summary ===
default cap: 16 MiB | test cap: 1 KiB
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 19 passed, 0 failed
```

```
[case 6] exec: UTF-8 byte boundary truncation
  ok: result.ok is true
  FAIL: stdout truncated
  FAIL: byte length stays near cap

=== Proof Summary ===
```

target.title: fix #98107: Gateway regenerates service-env file on every restart, wiping Telegram bot tokens
target.body:
Closes #98107

## Summary

- Preserve existing generated macOS LaunchAgent env-file values for config SecretRef environment keys when the install plan regenerates the gateway service environment.
- Track current config SecretRef env ids as managed service keys even when the current shell no longer contains the secret value.
- Keep fresh `.env` and current shell SecretRef values ahead of older generated env-file values.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running the gateway as a macOS LaunchAgent could lose Telegram bot token environment values after gateway service regeneration, causing Telegram startup to fail with invalid-token API errors after restart or update flows.

## Why This Change Was Made

The install-plan builder already receives parsed existing LaunchAgent env-file values and source provenance, but the managed render policy did not restore file-backed SecretRef values after deleting managed keys during regeneration. This change treats env ids referenced by current config SecretRefs as service-managed keys and restores only file-backed existing values for macOS LaunchAgent rendering when no fresher `.env` or shell SecretRef value is available.

## User Impact

Users who keep Telegram bot tokens in the generated LaunchAgent service env file no longer have those values replaced or dropped by placeholder config values during service-env regeneration. OpenClaw still avoids rendering ordinary config env values into the LaunchAgent env file, and stale inline service env values remain excluded.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** The LaunchAgent reader can parse `~/.openclaw/service-env/<label>.env` and mark entries as `file`, but `buildGatewayInstallPlan` only preserved non-managed existing env vars. During regeneration, `writeManagedServiceEnvKeysToEnvironment` removed managed keys and the render policy only re-added state-dir `.env` or current shell SecretRef values, so an existing generated env-file Telegram token was lost when the current shell did not contain it.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The fix restores existing values specifically from `file` / `inline-and-file` provenance for keys still referenced by current config SecretRefs, then lets state-dir `.env` and current shell SecretRef values override them. That addresses the regeneration source of truth without making ordinary inline service env or unrelated stale keys durable.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Gateway install-plan regeneration for a macOS LaunchAgent with an existing generated env-file Telegram SecretRef token and config placeholder value.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux source checkout invoking the actual production `buildGatewayInstallPlan` code path with `platform: "darwin"`, an executable wrapper, existing env-file source metadata, and current Telegram SecretRef config. No mocked planner was used in this proof command.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Ran a `node --import tsx` production-code probe from the repository root:

```shell
pnpm --dir /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/issue-98107 exec node --import tsx -e "import fs from 'node:fs'; import os from 'node:os'; import path from 'node:path'; import { buildGatewayInstallPlan } from './src/commands/daemon-install-helpers.ts'; const home = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'oc-98107-proof-')); try { const plan = await buildGatewayInstallPlan({ env: { HOME: home }, port: 3000, runtime: 'node', platform: 'darwin', wrapperPath: '/bin/sh', existingEnvironment: { TELEGRAM_DEFAULT_BOTTOKEN: 'existing-env-file-token', OPENCLAW_SERVICE_MANAGED_ENV_KEYS: 'OPENROUTER_API_KEY' }, existingEnvironmentValueSources: { TELEGRAM_DEFAULT_BOTTOKEN: 'file', OPENCLAW_SERVICE_MANAGED_ENV_KEYS: 'file' }, config: { env: { vars: { OPENROUTER_API_KEY: 'openrouter-placeholder', TELEGRAM_DEFAULT_BOTTOKEN: 'your-real-telegram-default-token-here' } }, channels: { telegram: { accounts: { default: { botToken: { source: 'env', provider: 'default', id: 'TELEGRAM_DEFAULT_BOTTOKEN' } } } } } } }); console.log(JSON.stringify({ preservedToken: plan.environment.TELEGRAM_DEFAULT_BOTTOKEN, managedKeys: plan.environment.OPENCLAW_SERVICE_MANAGED_ENV_KEYS, openrouterRendered: plan.environment.OPENROUTER_API_KEY ?? null, tokenValueSource: plan.environmentValueSources?.TELEGRAM_DEFAULT_BOTTOKEN }, null, 2)); } finally { fs.rmSync(home, { recursive: true, force: true }); }"
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```json
{
  "preservedToken": "existing-env-file-token",
  "managedKeys": "OPENROUTER_API_KEY,TELEGRAM_DEFAULT_BOTTOKEN",
  "openrouterRendered": null,
  "tokenValueSource": "file"
}
```

- **Observed result after fix:** The Telegram SecretRef value from the existing generated env file remains in the regenerated plan with `file` provenance, the placeholder config value is not rendered, and the key is added to `OPENCLAW_SERVICE_MANAGED_ENV_KEYS`.
- **What was not tested:** I did not run a live macOS `launchctl kickstart` / `openclaw gateway restart` cycle or call the real Telegram API from this Linux environment. Live macOS LaunchAgent and Telegram transport validation remains the proof gap.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/commands/daemon-install-helpers.test.ts`

```shell
pnpm --dir /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/issue-98107 test src/commands/daemon-install-helpers.test.ts
```

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  48 passed (48)
```

```shell
pnpm --dir /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/issue-98107 run format:check -- src/commands/daemon-install-helpers.ts src/commands/daemon-install-helpers.test.ts src/daemon/service-env-render-policy.ts
```

```text
All matched files use the correct format.
```

```shell
pnpm --dir /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/issue-98107 run tsgo:test:src
```

```text
PASS, exit code 0.
```

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** `merge-risk:config`, `merge-risk:service-install`, `impact:auth-provider`, `impact:message-loss`, `impact:crash-loop`.
- **Risk explanation:** The change affects gateway service environment regeneration and managed env key tracking. A wrong precedence order could keep stale values or overwrite fresher state-dir / shell values.
- **Why acceptable:** The restoration is limited to macOS LaunchAgent rendering, requires existing source provenance from the generated env file, and only applies to keys still referenced by current config SecretRefs. State-dir `.env` values and current shell SecretRef values continue to override existing file values, while ordinary config env placeholders remain unrendered.

## Patch quality notes

- **Fix classification:** Root-cause service-env regeneration fix with a focused regression test.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** Medium-high for the install-plan source of truth; live macOS LaunchAgent restart proof is still missing.
- **Patch quality notes:** The patch stays within the existing service env plan/render policy, keeps source provenance checks, and does not add Telegram-specific behavior or persist new secret storage.

target.title: fix(message): thread --limit through to CLI formatter and surface provider pagination hints
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #71452

`renderMessageList` in `src/commands/message-format.ts` hard-coded `messages.slice(0, 25)`, so `message read`, `message pins`, and `message search` always capped CLI table output at 25 rows regardless of `--limit`. Provider pagination signals (`hasMore`, `nextBatch`, `@odata.nextLink`) were silently discarded — users had no indication more results existed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three gaps in the end-to-end data flow:

1. **Formatter cap**: `renderMessageList` did not accept a caller-provided limit, defaulting to a hardcoded 25.
2. **CLI→Formatter bridge**: `messageCommand` parsed `--limit` and passed it to the provider, but never forwarded it to the formatter.
3. **Pagination visibility**: Providers (Slack/Matrix/MS Teams) already returned pagination metadata, but the CLI renderer never surfaced it.

This is a minimal fix — no heuristic hints, no return-value signature changes, no new abstractions.

### Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/commands/message-format.ts` | `FormatOpts` gains `displayLimit`; `renderMessageList` uses it (default 25); new `renderPaginationHint` emits one muted line when provider cursor signals exist (`hasMore` / `nextBatch` / `@odata.nextLink`); `formatMessageCliText` accepts optional `displayLimit` param; search branch compares `total_results > list.length` to distinguish completed searches from paginated ones |
| `src/commands/message.ts` | Parses `--limit` via `parsePositiveIntOrUndefined` and forwards it to `formatMessageCliText` |
| `src/commands/message-format.test.ts` (new) | 11 tests: displayLimit honored for read/pins/search, default 25, below-limit rendering, pagination hints for `hasMore` / `nextBatch` / `@odata.nextLink`, `total_results` exceeding vs equaling returned count |

## Why This Approach (vs #79593)

#79593 is the prior art (~400 LOC, CONFLICTING, unmaintained since May). This PR keeps the same core fix (displayLimit threading) while dropping the three controversial pieces:

- **No "Showing X of Y" truncation hint** — requires changing `renderMessageList`'s return signature
- **No "Reached --limit (N)" heuristic** — unreliable when the provider returned exactly the requested count (Discord has no `hasMore`)
- **No CHANGELOG.md edit** — release-owned file

## Evidence

- Tests: 11 formatter tests + 6 message tests, all passing
- oxlint: clean
- oxfmt: clean
- Live Matrix verification with `nextBatch`:

```
$ node openclaw.mjs message read --target '!room:server' --channel matrix

Messages
┌──────────────────┬──────────────┬──────────┬──────────┐
│ ...              │ ...          │ ...      │ ...      │
└──────────────────┴──────────────┴──────────┴──────────┘
More results available. Use --limit to fetch more, or --json for the raw cursor.
```

## User Impact

- **Before**: `openclaw message read --limit 50` rendered only 25 rows with no indication more existed. Provider pagination cursors (Matrix `nextBatch`, Slack `hasMore`, MS Teams `@odata.nextLink`) were invisible to CLI users. Discord search with `total_results` gave no hint of remaining matches.
- **After**: `--limit` is honored — `--limit 50` renders up to 50 rows. When the provider signals more results are available (any of `hasMore`, `nextBatch`, or `@odata.nextLink`), a muted hint line appears below the table. Discord search additionally checks `total_results > returned_count` so completed searches do not show a false hint.
- **Default behavior unchanged**: omitting `--limit` still defaults to 25 rows.
- **JSON output unchanged**: `--json` continues to carry raw provider payloads including cursor fields.

﻿Closes #98864

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Codex dynamic tool calls that provided only timeoutSeconds could miss the intended seconds-form hard-call bound and fall back to the default dynamic tool watchdog.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Codex app-server dynamic tool timeout resolvers now preserve timeoutMs precedence and treat numeric timeoutSeconds as the seconds-form fallback when timeoutMs is absent. The fallback adds a small wrapper grace window so tools that already own timeoutSeconds, such as sessions_send, can return their structured timeout result before the outer app-server watchdog aborts the bridge.

## User Impact

Long-running or bounded Codex dynamic tools can use seconds-form timeout values without silently falling back to the default watchdog, including both the primary Codex dynamic-tool path and the side-question dynamic-tool path.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: timeoutMs still wins; timeoutSeconds-only calls now set a seconds-derived app-server watchdog; invalid timeoutSeconds values are ignored; the existing failed response shape is used when the wrapper watchdog expires; a tool-owned timeoutSeconds result can return before the wrapper grace expires; the side-question sibling dynamic-tool timeout reader now honors timeoutSeconds with the same precedence and grace behavior.

target.title: fix(macos): preserve profile env in launch agent
target.body:
Fixes #98594.

## What Problem This Solves

The macOS app launch-at-login plist only preserved `PATH` in `EnvironmentVariables`. If a user enabled Launch at login while running OpenClaw with a custom profile, the login-launched app lost `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` and fell back to the default `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` profile.

## Why This Change Was Made

`OpenClawPaths` already treats `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` as the supported profile-selection contract. The app LaunchAgent now carries those two non-empty environment variables alongside `PATH` so the next login uses the same profile that was active when autostart was enabled.

The plist is generated through `PropertyListSerialization` instead of a hand-written XML string, so paths containing XML-sensitive characters are escaped by Foundation.

## User Impact

macOS users with custom OpenClaw profiles can enable Launch at login without silently switching back to the default profile on the next login.

## Evidence

- Added focused Swift coverage for:
  - preserving non-empty `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`
  - omitting blank profile env values
  - parsing the generated plist after XML-sensitive profile paths
- `git diff --cached --check` passed before commit.
- `swiftc -parse apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/LaunchAgentManager.swift` passed locally.

## Not Run Locally

- `swift test --package-path apps/macos --filter LaunchAgentManagerTests` could not run on this machine because the available Swift toolchain is 5.7.2 while `apps/macos/Package.swift` requires Swift tools 6.2; the command exits immediately with `XCTest not available`.
- Full Swift typecheck also cannot complete with this local Swift 5.7.2 toolchain because existing project sources use newer Swift syntax.
