target.title: fix(memory-host-sdk): prevent mid-transcript [cron:...] from wiping archive content
target.body:
<!--
Closes #98241
Related PR: #98246 (same root cause, similar approach)
-->

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who paste a cron log line or type `[cron:` as part of a question mid-conversation (after prior chat) lose all earlier archive content from `memory_search`. The wipe is silent — no error, no warning.

Affected surface: session archive processing in `buildSessionEntry` (called during gateway memory sync). When any user message matches the `^\[cron:[^\]]+\]\s*` regex, the entire collected archive content is reset to zero, making prior conversation history invisible to `memory_search`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing code had only `!generatedByCronRun` as a guard on the cron classification wipe block. Since the guard is set to true on first match and never reset, a single mid-transcript `[cron:...]` message would:
1. Match the regex content classifier
2. Clear all collected content
3. Cause ALL subsequent messages (including real assistant responses) to be skipped

Fix: two additive guards that restrict when the content-based classifier can fire:
- `!sessionStoreAlreadyClassifiedCron` — skip the heuristic when the session store already has authoritative cron classification
- `!hasSeenPriorUserMessage` — only classify as cron when `[cron:` appears on the very first user message (genuine cron transcripts always start with the cron prompt)

Mid-transcript `[cron:` matches still have their text sanitized via `sanitizeSessionText` but no longer cause cross-message data loss. Orphan cron archives (session-meta lost, `[cron:` IS the first user message) remain correctly opaque — the heuristic is identical to the old behavior for the first-message case.

Competitive PR #98246 targets the same root cause with the same approach. The code's own comment (session-files.ts:858-861) explicitly warned about this scenario.

## User Impact

Prevents silent data loss. Users who type `[cron:` prompts or paste cron output mid-session will keep full archive visibility in `memory_search`. Existing true cron-run archives (session-store classified, session-meta keyed, or first-message `[cron:`) are unaffected.

## Evidence

### 1. Unit test suite (38 tests, all pass)

```bash
pnpm test packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-files.test.ts
```

```text
 ✓ |unit-fast| session-files.test.ts > buildSessionEntry > indexes usage-counted reset/deleted archives
 ✓ |unit-fast| session-files.test.ts > buildSessionEntry > keeps cron-run deleted archives opaque
 ✓ |unit-fast| session-files.test.ts > buildSessionEntry > keeps cron-run reset archives opaque
 ✓ |unit-fast| session-files.test.ts > buildSessionEntry > does not wipe archive content when [cron:...] appears mid-transcript
 ✓ |unit-fast| session-files.test.ts > buildSessionEntry > strips inbound metadata
 ✓ |unit-fast| session-files.test.ts > buildSessionEntry > skips inter-session user messages

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  38 passed (38)
```

### 2. Multi-scenario verification (5 scenarios, production code path)

The `buildSessionEntry` function was called with realistic archive data covering all relevant edge cases. This is the exact same function the gateway calls during memory sync — no mocks, no stubs, built from the same TypeScript source compiled into the gateway dist.

**Real environment**: Linux 4.19.112 (x86_64), Node 24.13.1, OpenClaw dev checkout

```text
✓ |unit| proof-demo.test.ts > MID-TRANSCRIPT: [cron:...] after prior user msg does NOT wipe (THE FIX)
  [mid-transcript] contentLen=93 generatedByCronRun=undefined
  [mid-transcript] hasFirstMsg=true
  [mid-transcript] hasLastMsg=true
✓ |unit| proof-demo.test.ts > ORPHAN CRON: genuine cron archive stays opaque (no regression)
  [orphan-cron] generatedByCronRun=true
✓ |unit| proof-demo.test.ts > SESSION-STORE-CRON: store says cron → stays opaque
✓ |unit| proof-demo.test.ts > NORMAL: no cron text → content preserved
✓ |unit| proof-demo.test.ts > SESSION-STORE-NOT-CRON: not-cron store → not wiped

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  5 passed (5)
```

| # | Scenario | Expected | Result |
|---|----------|----------|--------|
| 1 | Mid-transcript `[cron:...]` after prior user message | Content preserved, NOT marked cron | ✅ |
| 2 | Genuine orphan cron archive (first msg is `[cron:...]`) | Opaque (marked cron) | ✅ |
| 3 | Session store says cron | Opaque via session-store guard | ✅ |
| 4 | Normal session, no cron text | Content fully preserved | ✅ |
| 5 | Session store says not-cron + no prior user cron match | Not wiped | ✅ |

### 3. Compiled gateway dist verification

The fix is confirmed present in the compiled production gateway bundle:

```text
✅ FIX CONFIRMED: Both guards are present in the compiled gateway dist.
   - sessionStoreAlreadyClassifiedCron: true (session-store guard)
```

target.title: fix(openai): bound Codex image generation no-body response reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a sibling OOM gap in OpenAI Codex OAuth image generation. The Codex Responses SSE path already bounds streamed bodies in `readResponseBodyText`, but the `!response.body` branch still called `response.text()` and only checked `MAX_CODEX_IMAGE_SSE_BYTES` after buffering the full payload. A faulty or hostile endpoint returning a body without a readable stream could still grow gateway memory without bound before the size guard fired.

## Why This Change Was Made

The no-body branch now fail-closes before any full-buffer fallback:

- reject oversized bodies from a trustworthy `Content-Length` header before calling `readResponseWithLimit` / `arrayBuffer()`
- reject missing or invalid `Content-Length` when no readable stream exists, instead of reading an unknown-size body
- only read bounded no-body payloads when `Content-Length` is present and within `MAX_CODEX_IMAGE_SSE_BYTES` (64 MiB)

This follows the same invariant as the existing streamed Codex image SSE guard:

- streamed Codex image SSE responses remain incrementally capped and cancelled on overflow
- no-body Codex image responses now reject early from `Content-Length` or fail closed when length is unknown
- loopback transport proof exercises the production Codex OAuth image path over real HTTP on `127.0.0.1`

## User Impact

Operators using Codex OAuth image generation through the Responses transport are protected when a provider returns an oversized or unknown-size payload on the no-body response path. Valid Codex image SSE responses continue to work unchanged.

## Evidence

Loopback transport proof: I ran the production Codex OAuth `generateImage` path against a local HTTP server on `127.0.0.1`. This uses the real `postJsonRequest` / `fetchWithSsrFGuard` path, real HTTP `Response` streams/headers, OAuth auth stubbing only, and no mocked `postJsonRequest`.

```text
$ node scripts/openclaw-openai-codex-image-loopback-proof.mjs
{
  "proof": "openai codex image loopback",
  "valid": {
    "mode": "valid-codex-image-sse-over-loopback",
    "ok": true,
    "images": 1,
    "cancelObserved": false,
    "payloadBytes": 277,
    "ms": 1490
  },
  "oversizedStream": {
    "mode": "oversized-stream-cancel-over-loopback",
    "ok": true,
    "error": "OpenAI Codex image generation response exceeded size limit",
    "cancelObserved": true,
    "payloadBytes": 70254592,
    "ms": 819
  },
  "oversizedNoBody": {
    "mode": "oversized-no-body-over-loopback",
    "ok": true,
    "error": "OpenAI Codex image generation response exceeded size limit",
    "bodyNullSimulated": true,
    "earlyReject": true,
    "arrayBufferCalled": false,
    "contentLengthBytes": 67108865,
    "payloadBytes": 67108865,
    "ms": 148
  }
}
```

Targeted unit proof: provider tests cover streamed overflow, no-body `Content-Length` early rejection without `arrayBuffer()`, and fail-closed behavior when `Content-Length` is missing.

```text
$ pnpm test extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.test.ts -t "rejects oversized Codex OAuth image responses without a readable body stream"
$ pnpm test extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.test.ts -t "rejects no-body Codex OAuth image responses without Content-Length"
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 64 skipped (65)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard
```

Loopback Vitest wrapper:

```text
$ pnpm test extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.loopback.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose
 ✓ extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.loopback.test.ts > OpenAI Codex image generation loopback proof > runs valid and oversized Codex image reads over loopback HTTP
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard
```

```text
$ pnpm dup:check:coverage
[dup:check] target coverage ok
$ pnpm run lint:tmp:no-raw-channel-fetch
# passed
```

Notes for reviewers:

- The no-body loopback case simulates `response.body === null` after a real loopback fetch and proves `earlyReject: true` with `arrayBufferCalled: false` when `Content-Length` exceeds the cap.
- Unknown-size no-body responses fail closed with `OpenAI Codex image generation response missing readable body stream`.

AI-assisted: built with Codex. I understand the change: it rejects no-body Codex image responses from `Content-Length` before buffering, fail-closes unknown-size no-body responses, and keeps streamed SSE reads incrementally bounded.

target.title: fix(discord): guard message handler against malformed gateway dispatch data
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Discord message handler in `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.ts` accesses `entry.data` and `last.data` properties without null safety, risking crashes at runtime when the gateway dispatches malformed or incomplete MESSAGE_CREATE data. The `shouldDebounce` callback also directly accesses `entry.data.message` without an optional chain, while the handler ingress had no guard to reject dispatches missing essential message data before reaching the debouncer.

Without these guards, a single malformed gateway dispatch event can crash the Discord message processing pipeline (`shouldDebounce` TypeError on undefined `entry.data`), causing message loss and requiring a gateway restart. The ingress guard ensures malformed dispatches are cleanly rejected at the earliest possible boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

A defensive programming audit identified 4 locations in the message handler where `entry.data` or `last.data` are accessed without null safety. ClawSweeper review further identified that malformed dispatches are not guarded before enqueue — the handler ingress lets malformed data through to `shouldDebounce`, which crashes on `entry.data.message` when `entry.data` is nullish. The review response adds an ingress guard, an optional chain in `shouldDebounce`, and a focused regression test.

## Summary

**Problem:** Malformed Discord MESSAGE_CREATE gateway dispatches with nullish or missing `data` / `message` properties crash the message handler at 6 access sites (buildKey, shouldDebounce, combined text builder, synthetic message, handler ingress). Without fixing all of them, a single bad dispatch can crash the entire pipeline.

**Solution:** Add null-safety (optional chaining and early returns) at all 6 access sites. The handler ingress guard (`if (!data.message?.id) return`) is the earliest rejection point — it prevents malformed dispatches from reaching replay claim, preflight, or the debouncer entirely.

What changed: +6 null-safety guards across `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.ts`, plus 1 regression test in `message-handler.queue.test.ts`.

What did NOT change: No changes to the gateway mapper (`gateway-dispatch.ts`), preflight logic, inbound replay/dedupe, message run queue, or any other module. No infrastructure files (`pnpm-lock.yaml`, `CHANGELOG.md`) are touched. No new dependencies are introduced.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Add null-safety to Discord message handler so malformed MESSAGE_CREATE gateway dispatches with missing message data do not crash the message processing pipeline.

**Real environment tested:** Local unit test environment with real function exports from `createDiscordMessageHandler` (not mocked internals). The test exercises both the malformed payload rejection path and the valid message processing path through the actual handler function.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
```bash
# node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run <test-file>
run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.queue.test.ts --reporter verbose
```

**After-fix evidence:**
```bash
# node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run <test-file> 2>&1
 ✓ |extension-discord| ... > handles malformed MESSAGE_CREATE data without blocking subsequent valid messages
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  23 passed (23)
```

BEFORE FIX: A malformed MESSAGE_CREATE payload with no `message` property would crash `shouldDebounce` at `entry.data.message` (TypeError on undefined `entry.data`), blocking all subsequent valid dispatches.

AFTER FIX: The handler ingress guard (`if (!data.message?.id) return`) rejects malformed dispatches before they reach the debouncer. A subsequent valid message processes normally through the same handler. The terminal output confirms all 23 tests pass.

**Observed result after the fix:** All 23 tests pass. The new regression test demonstrates that a malformed MESSAGE_CREATE payload (`{ channel_id: "ch-1" }` with no `message` property) is cleanly rejected by the ingress guard and does not reach preflight or message processing. A subsequent valid message is still processed normally, confirming the guard does not block legitimate dispatches.

**What was not tested:** Real Discord gateway runtime (L3). This PR cannot provide live Discord gateway logs because it requires a running Discord bot with a valid token and real WebSocket connection — the author's setup does not include a Discord development bot environment. The malformed gateway dispatch scenario is a defensive/hypothetical boundary case, not a reproduced production failure. The L2 unit test evidence correctly exercises the real function exports with both malformed and valid data paths.

## Risk checklist

- [x] **merge-risk: 🚨 message-delivery** — Risk: Medium. The diff touches Discord inbound message handling. Mitigation: The ingress guard and optional chains are additive null-safety that only skip malformed dispatches — they cannot introduce new failure paths for valid dispatches. The regression test confirms valid messages still process normally through the same handler.
- [x] Changes limited to `extensions/discord/src/monitor/` — no cross-boundary or infrastructure impact.
- [x] No `pnpm-lock.yaml` or `CHANGELOG.md` changes.
- [x] +40/-1 lines across 2 files (1 source, 1 test), no new dependencies.
- [x] All existing tests pass with no regressions.
- [x] New regression test covers the malformed payload drop path.

target.title: fix(memory-wiki): prevent distinct titles from silently overwriting each other
target.body:
## Summary

Two distinct memory-wiki pages whose titles slugify to the same value silently overwrite each other, and the first page is permanently lost.

The agent-facing path is `wiki_apply` with op `create_synthesis`. When an agent saves a synthesis titled "Q3 Report" and later saves a different synthesis titled "Q3-Report", both resolve to `syntheses/q3-report.md` under id `synthesis.q3-report`. The second write overwrites the first: the first synthesis's managed Summary, sourceIds, claims, and confidence are gone, and neither `wiki_get` nor `wiki_search` can recover them. No error or warning is surfaced.

`slugifyWikiSegment` collapses case, spaces, and punctuation, so realistic agent-generated titles collide: "Q3 Report" / "Q3-Report", "Project Alpha!" / "Project Alpha", "Sales (2026)" / "Sales 2026", "Meeting Notes" / "meeting notes". The sibling CLI path `wiki ingest` has the same defect for `sources/<slug>.md`.

## Root cause

`extensions/memory-wiki/src/apply.ts` derived the synthesis page path and id from the bare slug, with no disambiguation when an existing page at that slug belongs to a different title:

```ts
// before
const slug = slugifyWikiSegment(params.mutation.title);
const pagePath = path.join("syntheses", `${slug}.md`).replace(/\\/g, "/");
const root = await fsRoot(params.config.vault.path);
const existing = await root.readText(pagePath).catch(() => "");
```

`slugifyWikiSegment` only appends a hash when the slug exceeds the byte cap (`extensions/memory-wiki/src/markdown.ts`), so short colliding titles get no hash. `ingest.ts` had the identical pattern for `source.<slug>`.

## Fix

Add one shared identity helper and route both writers through it. The plain readable slug is reused when it is free or already owns the same title (so re-applying a synthesis still updates in place); a distinct title that lands on an existing page gets a stable title-hash suffix, matching the existing `okf.ts` hashed-identity pattern:

```ts
// after (markdown.ts)
export async function resolveTitleKeyedWikiSlug(params: {
  title: string;
  readExistingTitleBySlug: (slug: string) => Promise<string | undefined>;
}): Promise<string> {
  const baseSlug = slugifyWikiSegment(params.title);
  const existingTitle = await params.readExistingTitleBySlug(baseSlug);
  if (existingTitle === undefined || existingTitle.trim() === params.title.trim()) {
    return baseSlug;
  }
  const suffix = createHash("sha1").update(params.title).digest("hex").slice(0, WIKI_SEGMENT_HASH_BYTES);
  return `${baseSlug}-${suffix}`;
}
```

`apply.ts` (`create_synthesis`) and `ingest.ts` (`wiki ingest`) both resolve their slug through this helper before reading/writing the page.

The "existing title" is read the same way query and compile resolve a page's effective title (`extensions/memory-wiki/src/markdown.ts`): frontmatter `title`, then the first `# ` H1 heading, then the file name. So a page that occupies the target slug but has no frontmatter (a supported hand-authored raw source page) is recognized as occupied and gets a distinct slug for the incoming title instead of being silently overwritten. The helper also canonicalizes the title once (trimmed) and uses that single value for the base slug, the existing-title comparison, and the hash suffix, so two writes of the same logical title that differ only by surrounding whitespace land on the same page instead of forking a duplicate.

## Why this is the right boundary

- The helper lives next to `slugifyWikiSegment` and reuses the same `WIKI_SEGMENT_HASH_BYTES` and SHA-1 pattern already used by `okf.ts`/`createWikiPageFilename`. Two call sites share it (synthesis and source), so it pays rent.
- Backward compatible with no vault migration: the common single-page-per-title case keeps its plain `<slug>.md` path because the stored title matches. Only genuine distinct-title collisions get a hashed path, so existing vaults and same-title re-applies are unchanged.
- Covers both managed and unmanaged pages: collision detection compares the incoming title against the existing page's effective title (frontmatter title, else H1, else file name), so a no-frontmatter raw source page is protected, not just generated pages that carry a `title` field.
- Prior art: closed PR #65992 proposed a source-path-keyed fix for the ingest half only and was closed unmerged; merged PR #64742 fixed only the Unicode/empty-slug case. Neither touched `create_synthesis`, and the distinct-title slug collision is still live on current `main` (proof below). This change fixes the agent-facing synthesis path that no prior PR addressed, and removes the same live collision from the source path with one helper.

## Verification

From a worktree with deps (node at /opt/node/bin):

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-wiki/src/slug-collision.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/wiki-notes-read-retry.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/apply.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/ingest.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/markdown.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/query.test.ts` -> 72 passed
- `slug-collision.test.ts` regressions fail on pristine `main` and pass with this patch: distinct synthesis titles, distinct ingest titles, a no-frontmatter raw source page colliding with a generated ingest title, and a colliding title re-applied with surrounding whitespace updating its existing hashed page instead of duplicating it.
- `wiki-notes-read-retry.test.ts` regressions fail on previous PR head 499bffe00e and pass with this patch: transient title-read failures during colliding synthesis creation and source ingest still allocate the distinct hash-suffixed page instead of reusing the occupied bare slug.
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint extensions/memory-wiki/src/apply.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/ingest.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/markdown.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/slug-collision.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/wiki-notes-read-retry.test.ts` -> clean
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/memory-wiki/src/apply.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/ingest.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/markdown.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/slug-collision.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/wiki-notes-read-retry.test.ts` -> clean
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p extensions/memory-wiki/tsconfig.json` -> exit 0
- Branch rebased onto current `origin/main` 76ccd17ac3.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: distinct memory-wiki syntheses and ingested sources whose titles slugify to the same value no longer overwrite each other and silently lose the first page.
Real environment tested: drove the real `applyMemoryWikiMutation` (`create_synthesis`) and the real `ingestMemoryWikiSource` (`wiki ingest`) against temp vaults read from disk after each run, on pristine main at origin/main 9ff7abc8989c1770856b27d5b06e6bb6695ce666 with the original production files restored, on previous PR head 499bffe00e with the retry repair absent, and on PR head f7ca15a483 with this patch applied, identical inputs for each before/after pair. The transient-read run injected one filesystem `ENOENT` at the existing source page read boundary; all vault writes, page parsing, slug resolution, and disk reads stayed production code.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: apply `create_synthesis` "Q3 Report" (body "Revenue grew 12 percent", source.finance, claim.q3.revenue), then apply `create_synthesis` "Q3-Report" (body "Headcount fell 4 percent"); separately `wiki ingest` "Q3 Report" then "Q3-Report"; ingest "Q3 Report" onto a pre-seeded hand-authored no-frontmatter sources/q3-report.md; re-apply "  Q3-Report  "; then run `wiki ingest` "Q3 Report" followed by `wiki ingest` "Q3-Report" while the first read of the occupied `sources/q3-report.md` returns `ENOENT`; list each directory and read each page from disk.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine origin/main, three prod files reverted, driver identical)
create_synthesis distinct titles 'Q3 Report' then 'Q3-Report'
  first  pagePath=syntheses/q3-report.md
  second pagePath=syntheses/q3-report.md
  synthesis page files (count=1): ["q3-report.md"]
  first synthesis body keeps 'Revenue grew 12 percent': false
  first synthesis body keeps source 'source.finance': false
  wiki_search('Revenue grew 12 percent') recovers first synthesis: false
wiki ingest distinct titles 'Q3 Report' then 'Q3-Report'
  source page files (count=1): ["q3-report.md"]
  ingest A page keeps 'finance source body': false
ingest onto hand-authored no-frontmatter sources/q3-report.md
  ingest wrote to: sources/q3-report.md
  hand-authored q3-report.md keeps 'Hand authored raw source.': false

# AFTER (this patch, head 888df0ffcfecdce17a9b6c577b7d71f3109c02a9, identical inputs)
create_synthesis distinct titles 'Q3 Report' then 'Q3-Report'
  first  pagePath=syntheses/q3-report.md
  second pagePath=syntheses/q3-report-97358135a013.md
  synthesis page files (count=2): ["q3-report-97358135a013.md","q3-report.md"]
  first synthesis body keeps 'Revenue grew 12 percent': true
  first synthesis body keeps source 'source.finance': true
  wiki_search('Revenue grew 12 percent') recovers first synthesis: true
wiki ingest distinct titles 'Q3 Report' then 'Q3-Report'
  source page files (count=2): ["q3-report-97358135a013.md","q3-report.md"]
  ingest A page keeps 'finance source body': true
  ingest B page keeps 'headcount source body': true
ingest onto hand-authored no-frontmatter sources/q3-report.md
  ingest wrote to: sources/q3-report-4d84a9cac68c.md
  hand-authored q3-report.md keeps 'Hand authored raw source.': true
re-apply '  Q3-Report  ' (whitespace variant of existing 'Q3-Report')
  re-apply wrote to: syntheses/q3-report-97358135a013.md
  updates the existing hashed page in place, no duplicate: true
  synthesis page files (count): ["q3-report-97358135a013.md","q3-report.md"]

# BEFORE (previous PR head 499bffe00e, transient source title read)
first pagePath=sources/q3-report.md
second pagePath=sources/q3-report.md
injected transient read failure: true
source page files (count=1): ["q3-report.md"]
first page keeps finance source body: false
second page keeps headcount source body: true

# AFTER (this patch, head f7ca15a483, identical transient source title read)
first pagePath=sources/q3-report.md
second pagePath=sources/q3-report-97358135a013.md
injected transient read failure: true
source page files (count=2): ["q3-report-97358135a013.md","q3-report.md"]
first page keeps finance source body: true
second page keeps headcount source body: true
```
Observed result after fix: on pristine main both distinct titles collapse onto one bare-slug page, the first synthesis body and source.finance are gone, neither wiki_search nor the on-disk page can recover them, and a real ingest overwrites a hand-authored raw page; on the previous PR head a transient existing-page title read still makes the colliding source write back to the occupied bare slug and lose the first body; after the patch the second distinct title gets a stable title-hash slug, both pages persist with their own body and sources even after the transient read failure, search recovers the first synthesis, the hand-authored raw page is left intact, and re-applying the same title with only surrounding whitespace updates the existing hashed page in place instead of forking a duplicate.
What was not tested: no full `pnpm check` or `pnpm build` (OOM-prone box); two ingested sources given an identical explicit title still merge by design, since the trimmed title is the page identity here.

target.title: fix(browser): bound Playwright response body reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem:** `responseBodyViaPlaywright` calls `resp.text()` which decodes the entire response string (OOM risk on multi-MB responses).

**Solution:** Replace with `buf.subarray(0, maxBytes)` decode window — full Buffer allocation stays but full-string decoding is bounded. Same memory-bound guarantee without CDP complexity.

**What changed:** Removed CDP `Fetch.takeResponseBodyAsStream` path entirely (page-delivery truncation issue). Unified to single `body()+subarray()` path for all browsers (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit).

**What did NOT change:** Public API, return types, existing caller behavior, browser support matrix.

## What Problem This Solves

`responseBodyViaPlaywright` previously used `resp.text()` which loads the entire response as a JavaScript string (unbounded memory allocation) before checking `maxChars`. On a 500 MB response this allocated 500 MB+ string before truncation.

`resp.body()` returns a `Buffer` (Node.js native, no encoding cost). Combined with `buf.subarray(0, maxBytes)`, only the bounded prefix is decoded to string — the full 500 MB allocation becomes a 500 MB Buffer + ~800 KB string instead of a 500 MB string.

## Why This Change Was Made

The original PR introduced CDP `Fetch.takeResponseBodyAsStream` for truly bounded memory capture (no full Buffer). However, CDP intercept-at-Response-stage forces `Fetch.fulfillRequest` with the captured (truncated) body, which disrupts page network behavior — the page receives a bounded prefix instead of the original response. This is fundamental to CDP's design: once the body is taken from the stream, the original response can't be forwarded.

Removing the CDP path eliminates this class of bug entirely:
- Page always receives the original response (body, status, headers untouched)
- No CDP session management (Fetch.enable/disable, cleanup timing)
- Single code path for all browsers (simpler to maintain)
- 200 lines of CDP code deleted, 4 CDP-specific tests deleted

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Verify `resp.body()` + `buf.subarray(0, maxBytes)` returns a bounded text body while the page receives the original response.

**Real environment tested:** Node.js 22 with Vitest, Playwright browser test harness. Code path: `page.on('response')` → `resp.body()` → `Buffer.subarray(0, maxBytes)` → `TextDecoder.decode()`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
pnpm test extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.waits-next-download-saves-it.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence:**

BEFORE FIX — CDP `Fetch.takeResponseBodyAsStream` + `Fetch.fulfillRequest`: 200 lines, CDP intercepts at Response stage → page receives truncated body

AFTER FIX — `body()` + `subarray()`: 80 lines, no interception → page receives original response untouched

Real browser proof (Playwright Chromium, Google Chrome 138, headless, via `page.on('response')` passive observer):

```bash
# node browser-proof.mjs
SERVER=http://127.0.0.1:43573

| Metric              | Tool (body()+subarray) | Page JS (full response) |
|---------------------|------------------------|-------------------------|
| Status              | 200                    | 200                     |
| Body length         | 8000 chars (bounded)   | 520000 chars (original) |
| Truncated?          | true                   | No                      |
| Original response   | 520000 chars           | 520000 chars            |

Verdict:
Tool returns bounded prefix (8000 < 520000): ✅
Page receives full original body (520000 === 520000): ✅
Page receives correct status (200): ✅
page.on('response') is passive — page delivery unaffected: ✅
```

**Observed result after the fix:** All 15 tests pass. `resp.body()` is called but only `subarray(0, maxBytes)` is decoded to string. No page delivery disruption — the code is a passive observer via `page.on('response')`.

**What was not tested:** Extremely large responses (>500 MB) — `resp.body()` still allocates a full Buffer, which is a memory cost we accept vs. the full-string cost of `resp.text()`. CDP-level zero-copy capture was removed because it can't preserve page delivery.

## Tests and validation

- **15 tests pass** covering: bounded decode for small/large/chunked responses, negative control (text() would decode full body), mutation test (subarray bounded regardless of Buffer size)
- **Lint clean** (`npx oxlint`)
- **128 lines added, 580 removed** across source + test files

## Risk checklist

- **Risk level:** Low — removed the risky CDP path, unified to passive observer pattern.
- **Mitigation:** No CDP session management. No Fetch domain manipulation. No page response interception.
- **Merge-risk explanation:** None — removed the code that caused the merge risk (CDP fulfill path). No config/env/API changes.
- **User-visible behavior change?** No.
- **Config/env/migration change?** No.
- **Security/auth/network change?** No.

## Linked context

Pattern from PR #98496 (bounded response body reads to prevent OOM). CDP approach attempted in earlier revisions of this PR, removed after ClawSweeper review identified page-delivery truncation.

target.title: fix(discord): gate replyTo on first chunk for implicit-first replies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

With `channels.discord.replyToMode: "first"`, chunked replies send the native
Discord reply reference on ALL physical chunks, not just the first.  The
replied-to person gets N reply notifications for one logical answer.

Closes #99068

## Root Cause / Fix

In `sendDiscordText`, the `sendChunk` closure captures `replyTo` and passes it
unconditionally to every chunk body.  The `isFirst` flag controls components
and embeds but never gates `replyTo`.

Fix: add `suppressTrailingReply` flag (default `false` = backward compatible).
When `true`, gate `replyTo` on the first chunk only.  The flag is plumbed
through `sendDiscordText`, `sendDiscordMedia`, and `sendMessageDiscord` opts.

This preserves `replyTo` on all chunks for explicit reply tags and `"all"`
mode, while suppressing trailing chunks only for implicit single-use
(`"first"`) replies — matching ClawSweeper's guidance.

Also fix `sendDiscordMedia` trailing-chunk loop to pass `undefined` instead
of the inherited `replyTo`.

## Evidence

### Before (main — bug)

```
it("preserves reply reference across all text chunks")
  → ALL chunks get message_reference (bug for first mode)
```

### After (fix)

```
it("gates implicit-first reply to first text chunk only (#99068)")
  → first chunk: reply ✅  trailing chunk: undefined ✅

it("gates implicit-first reply to media caption chunk only (#99068)")
  → media caption: reply ✅  trailing text: undefined ✅

it("preserves reply across all text chunks for explicit/all mode")
  → all chunks: reply ✅

it("always suppresses reply on media trailing text chunks")
  → media caption: reply ✅  trailing: undefined ✅
```

### Test runner

```
  Tests  46 passed (46)
```

### Pre-submit

```

oxlint         ✓
git diff --check ✓
```

- [x] Discord channel (send layer)

target.title: fix(message): thread --limit through to CLI formatter and surface provider pagination hints
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #71452

`renderMessageList` in `src/commands/message-format.ts` hard-coded `messages.slice(0, 25)`, so `message read`, `message pins`, and `message search` always capped CLI table output at 25 rows regardless of `--limit`. Provider pagination signals (`hasMore`, `nextBatch`, `@odata.nextLink`) were silently discarded — users had no indication more results existed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three gaps in the end-to-end data flow:

1. **Formatter cap**: `renderMessageList` did not accept a caller-provided limit, defaulting to a hardcoded 25.
2. **CLI→Formatter bridge**: `messageCommand` parsed `--limit` and passed it to the provider, but never forwarded it to the formatter.
3. **Pagination visibility**: Providers (Slack/Matrix/MS Teams) already returned pagination metadata, but the CLI renderer never surfaced it.

This is a minimal fix — no heuristic hints, no return-value signature changes, no new abstractions.

### Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/commands/message-format.ts` | `FormatOpts` gains `displayLimit`; `renderMessageList` uses it (default 25); new `renderPaginationHint` emits one muted line when provider cursor signals exist (`hasMore` / `nextBatch` / `@odata.nextLink`); `formatMessageCliText` accepts optional `displayLimit` param; search branch compares `total_results > list.length` to distinguish completed searches from paginated ones |
| `src/commands/message.ts` | Parses `--limit` via `parsePositiveIntOrUndefined` and forwards it to `formatMessageCliText` |
| `src/commands/message-format.test.ts` (new) | 11 tests: displayLimit honored for read/pins/search, default 25, below-limit rendering, pagination hints for `hasMore` / `nextBatch` / `@odata.nextLink`, `total_results` exceeding vs equaling returned count |

## Why This Approach (vs #79593)

#79593 is the prior art (~400 LOC, CONFLICTING, unmaintained since May). This PR keeps the same core fix (displayLimit threading) while dropping the three controversial pieces:

- **No "Showing X of Y" truncation hint** — requires changing `renderMessageList`'s return signature
- **No "Reached --limit (N)" heuristic** — unreliable when the provider returned exactly the requested count (Discord has no `hasMore`)
- **No CHANGELOG.md edit** — release-owned file

## Evidence

- Tests: 11 formatter tests + 6 message tests, all passing
- oxlint: clean
- oxfmt: clean
- Live Matrix verification with `nextBatch`:

```
$ node openclaw.mjs message read --target '!room:server' --channel matrix

Messages
┌──────────────────┬──────────────┬──────────┬──────────┐
│ ...              │ ...          │ ...      │ ...      │
└──────────────────┴──────────────┴──────────┴──────────┘
More results available. Use --limit to fetch more, or --json for the raw cursor.
```

## User Impact

- **Before**: `openclaw message read --limit 50` rendered only 25 rows with no indication more existed. Provider pagination cursors (Matrix `nextBatch`, Slack `hasMore`, MS Teams `@odata.nextLink`) were invisible to CLI users. Discord search with `total_results` gave no hint of remaining matches.
- **After**: `--limit` is honored — `--limit 50` renders up to 50 rows. When the provider signals more results are available (any of `hasMore`, `nextBatch`, or `@odata.nextLink`), a muted hint line appears below the table. Discord search additionally checks `total_results > returned_count` so completed searches do not show a false hint.
- **Default behavior unchanged**: omitting `--limit` still defaults to 25 rows.
- **JSON output unchanged**: `--json` continues to carry raw provider payloads including cursor fields.

target.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)
target.body:
## Summary

`openclaw cron run` (manual/debug runs) on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes the job on success — consuming the one-shot and preventing its scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate `consecutiveErrors`/`consecutiveSkipped` counters, interfering with scheduled retry/backoff state.

This PR adds an `isManual` flag to `applyJobResult` so manual runs preserve the job and leave scheduled execution state untouched.

## Root cause

`applyJobResult()` has no concept of manual vs scheduled runs. When a manual run succeeds on a `deleteAfterRun: true` at-job, `shouldDelete` evaluates to `true` and the job is removed from the store — the scheduled fire never happens.

Additionally, manual error/skipped/success outcomes unconditionally mutate `consecutiveErrors` and `consecutiveSkipped` counters, which control retry backoff and auto-disable behavior for scheduled runs.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `timer.ts` | Add `isManual` option to `applyJobResult`; skip `deleteAfterRun` for manual runs; guard all counter mutations and alert emissions with `!isManual` |
| `ops.ts` | Pass `isManual: true` from manual run completion and invalid-persisted-run handling |
| `timer.regression.test.ts` | 5 new tests: manual ok/error preserve job, manual doesn't increment/reset counters |

## Tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts
 ✓ cron (45 tests) 144ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  45 passed (45)
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Manual `cron run` on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes it, preventing scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate scheduled retry counters.
- **Real environment tested**: Local OpenClaw checkout at `aa92a4a5b0`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0.

### Source-level proof

```
Main branch applyJobResult():
  - shouldDelete = kind === "at" && deleteAfterRun && status === "ok"
    → no manual discriminator, always deletes on success
  - consecutiveErrors incremented unconditionally on error
  - consecutiveSkipped incremented unconditionally on skip

Fix branch:
  - shouldDelete = wouldDelete && !opts?.isManual
    → manual runs never trigger deletion
  - Counter mutations guarded: if (!opts?.isManual) { ... }
    → manual runs don't affect retry/backoff state
```

### Regression test coverage

```
✅ manual ok on deleteAfterRun at-job → job preserved, not deleted
✅ manual error on deleteAfterRun at-job → job preserved, not deleted  
✅ scheduled ok on deleteAfterRun at-job → job deleted (unchanged behavior)
✅ manual error does not increment consecutiveErrors (pre-existing=3 → still 3)
✅ manual success does not reset consecutiveErrors (pre-existing=3 → still 3)
```

- **What was not tested**: Live `openclaw cron run` CLI flow (requires a running gateway with a configured `deleteAfterRun` at-job). The `isManual` flag propagation from `ops.ts` to `applyJobResult` is validated at the unit level.

Closes #83538


### Re-verification (2026-05-20)

Local checkout at `d89f14de26`, macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`.

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts

 ✓ cron  ../../src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts (39 tests) 116ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  39 passed (39)
   Duration  152ms
```

Full cron suite (`src/cron/`) also run: 94 test files, 901 passed. The 7 failures are in unrelated files (`run-log.test.ts`, `service.failure-alert.test.ts`) pre-existing on upstream/main.


## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: `openclaw cron run` (manual) of a `deleteAfterRun: true` at-job incorrectly deletes the job. Manual runs also pollute `consecutiveErrors`/`consecutiveSkipped` counters.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched checkout at `0cec2acc7a`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0.
- **Failing proof before fix**: On `upstream/main`, counter mutations and `shouldDelete` run unconditionally — no `isManual` discriminator exists.
- **Exact steps after patch**: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts` + `src/cron/service.failure-alert.test.ts`
- **Evidence after fix**: 46/46 timer regression tests pass (including 7 new #83538/#83933-specific tests). 7/7 failure-alert tests pass.
- **What was not tested**: Live Gateway CLI flow; the tests exercise the same `applyJobResult` code path the Gateway calls internally.

### Key test results

| Scenario | Result |
|----------|--------|
| Manual run + deleteAfterRun + success | NOT deleted ✅ |
| Scheduled run + deleteAfterRun + success | Deleted ✅ |
| Manual error + consecutiveErrors=3 | Stays 3 ✅ |
| Manual success + consecutiveErrors=5 | Stays 5 ✅ |
| Manual error → failure alert | NOT triggered ✅ |
| Scheduled error → failure alert | Triggered ✅ |


## Real behavior proof (Docker, 2026-05-21)

**Environment**: Docker container, `node:24-bookworm-slim` (aarch64), patched source at `885d605e56`.

### Latest fixes

| Issue | Problem | Fix |
|-------|---------|-----|
| P1 | Manual at-job error was disabling job (`enabled=false`, `nextRunAtMs=undefined`) | At-job error retry/disable block now guarded with `if (opts?.isManual)` |
| P2 | Manual success was clearing `lastFailureAlertAtMs` cooldown | Cooldown clearing now inside `if (!opts?.isManual)` guard |

### Test results

| Test Suite | Result |
|------------|--------|
| Timer regression (49 tests) | ✅ All passed |
| Failure-alert (7 tests) | ✅ All passed |

### Key verified behaviors

| Scenario | Result |
|----------|--------|
| Manual at-job error | `enabled` stays true, `nextRunAtMs` preserved ✅ |
| Manual success | `lastFailureAlertAtMs` cooldown preserved ✅ |
| Manual run + deleteAfterRun | Job NOT deleted ✅ |
| Scheduled run + deleteAfterRun | Job deleted ✅ |
| Manual error + consecutiveErrors=3 | Stays 3 ✅ |
| Manual success + consecutiveErrors=5 | Stays 5 ✅ |


## Real CLI proof (Docker Gateway, 2026-05-21)

**Environment**: Docker `node:24-bookworm-slim` (aarch64), patched Gateway at `885d605e56` running with `--allow-unconfigured`.

**Terminal transcript**: `openclaw cron add` → `cron show` → `cron run` (manual, triggers error) → `cron show` (job still exists, enabled=true, nextRunAtMs preserved) → `cron list` (job present) → `cron runs` (run history with error status, nextRunAtMs unchanged).

| Step | Command | Result |
|------|---------|--------|
| Add job | `openclaw cron add --name proof-job --at ... --delete-after-run` | Created with `deleteAfterRun: true` |
| Manual run | `openclaw cron run <id>` | `{"ok": true, "enqueued": true}` |
| After run | `openclaw cron show <id>` | `enabled: true`, `nextRunAtMs: preserved` ✅ |
| Job exists | `openclaw cron list` | Job still listed ✅ |
| Run history | `openclaw cron runs --id <id>` | `status: "error"`, `nextRunAtMs: preserved` ✅ |


## Real CLI proof at head SHA `642c3450d9` (Docker Gateway, 2026-05-21)

**Environment**: Docker `node:24-bookworm-slim` (aarch64), patched Gateway built from PR head.

| Test | Command | Before (main) | After (PR head) |
|------|---------|---------------|-----------------|
| A: at-job deleteAfterRun | `cron run` → `cron show` | Job deleted/disabled | `enabled: true`, `nextRunAtMs` preserved ✅ |
| B: every-job manual error | `cron run` → `cron show` | `nextRunAtMs` rewritten by backoff | `nextRunAtMs` unchanged ✅ |
| A+B: counters | `cron runs` | `consecutiveErrors` mutated | Unchanged ✅ |

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Manual `cron run` no longer consumes `deleteAfterRun` one-shot jobs, and no longer perturbs retry counters, at-job retry/disable state, recurring backoff, or failure-alert cooldown.
- **Real environment tested**: Docker container built from PR HEAD `3d32c9baff`, Linux aarch64 (OrbStack), Node.js `v24.14.0`, Vitest `v4.1.7`.
- **Failing proof before fix**: On upstream/main, `applyJobResult` has no manual-run discriminator — manual runs unconditionally drive `deleteAfterRun`, counter mutations, at-job disable, recurring backoff, and alert cooldown. The 12 regression tests added by this PR do not exist on main.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
# Build Docker image from PR HEAD
docker build --target build -t openclaw-pr83933:test .

# Test 1: Timer regression tests (includes all 12 manual-run isolation tests)
docker run --rm openclaw-pr83933:test node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts

# Test 2: Failure alert tests (adapted for manual-run isolation)
docker run --rm openclaw-pr83933:test node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service.failure-alert.test.ts

# Test 3: Lint check
docker run --rm openclaw-pr83933:test npx oxlint src/cron/service/timer.ts src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts src/cron/service.failure-alert.test.ts src/cron/service/ops.ts

# Test 4: Full cron test suite
docker run --rm openclaw-pr83933:test node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/
```

- **Evidence after fix**:

Test 1 — Timer regression: **55 tests passed** (284ms)
```
 ✓ cron src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts (55 tests) 284ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  55 passed (55)
```

Test 2 — Failure alert: **10 tests passed** (63ms)
```
 ✓ cron src/cron/service.failure-alert.test.ts (10 tests) 63ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
```

Test 3 — Lint: **0 errors, 0 warnings**
```
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
Finished in 13ms on 4 files with 189 rules using 10 threads.
```

Test 4 — Full cron suite: **1000 tests passed** across 98 test files
```
 Test Files  1 failed | 97 passed (98)
      Tests  2 failed | 1000 passed (1002)
```
The 2 failures are in `cron-protocol-conformance.test.ts` — these look for Swift source files (`apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/CronModels.swift`) which are not present in the Docker build target. These failures are pre-existing and unrelated to this PR.

- **Observed result after fix**: All 12 new regression tests pass, confirming that manual runs preserve one-shot jobs (`deleteAfterRun`), do not increment/reset counters, do not disable at-jobs on error, do not rewrite recurring `nextRunAtMs` with backoff, and do not clear failure-alert cooldown. Control-group tests confirm scheduled runs still drive all 5 state effects normally.

- **What was not tested**: Live Gateway CLI `openclaw cron run` end-to-end (covered by earlier Docker CLI proof at `642c3450d9` — subsequent commits were formatting-only changes via oxfmt). The `cron-protocol-conformance` tests require macOS app source and cannot run in Docker.


## Real behavior proof (Docker, HEAD `6bc3b9e374`, 2026-05-30)

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Manual `cron run` no longer consumes `deleteAfterRun` one-shot jobs, and no longer perturbs retry counters, at-job retry/disable state, recurring backoff, failure-alert cooldown, or skipped-run alert counters.
- **Real environment tested**: Docker container built from PR HEAD `6bc3b9e374`, Linux aarch64 (OrbStack), Node.js `v24.14.0`, Vitest `v4.1.7`.
- **Failing proof before fix**: On upstream/main, `applyJobResult` has no manual-run discriminator — manual runs unconditionally drive all 5 scheduled-state effects plus skipped-run alert paths. The 14 regression tests added by this PR do not exist on main.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
# Build Docker image from PR HEAD
docker build --target build -t openclaw-pr83933:test .

# Test 1: Timer regression tests (all 14 manual-run isolation tests)
docker run --rm openclaw-pr83933:test node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts

# Test 2: Failure alert tests (adapted for manual-run isolation)
docker run --rm openclaw-pr83933:test node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service.failure-alert.test.ts

# Test 3: Lint check
docker run --rm openclaw-pr83933:test npx oxlint src/cron/service/timer.ts src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts src/cron/service.failure-alert.test.ts src/cron/service/ops.ts

# Test 4: Full cron test suite
docker run --rm openclaw-pr83933:test node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/
```

- **Evidence after fix**:

Test 1 — Timer regression: **56 tests passed** (234ms)
```
 ✓ cron src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts (56 tests) 234ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  56 passed (56)
```

Test 2 — Failure alert: **11 tests passed** (92ms)
```
 ✓ cron src/cron/service.failure-alert.test.ts (11 tests) 92ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  11 passed (11)
```

Test 3 — Lint: **0 errors, 0 warnings**
```
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
Finished in 10ms on 4 files with 189 rules using 10 threads.
```

Test 4 — Full cron suite: **1002 tests passed** across 98 test files
```
 Test Files  1 failed | 97 passed (98)
      Tests  2 failed | 1002 passed (1004)
```
The 2 failures are in `cron-protocol-conformance.test.ts` — these look for Swift source files (`apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/CronModels.swift`) which are not present in the Docker build target. Pre-existing and unrelated to this PR.

- **Observed result after fix**: All 14 new regression tests pass, covering all 6 guarded state effects including the newly-added manual skipped-run isolation:
  - Manual `deleteAfterRun` at-job → NOT deleted ✅
  - Manual error → counters NOT incremented ✅
  - Manual success → counters NOT reset, cooldown NOT cleared ✅
  - Manual at-job error → NOT disabled, nextRunAtMs preserved ✅
  - Manual every-job error → backoff NOT applied, nextRunAtMs preserved ✅
  - Manual skipped at-job → consecutiveSkipped NOT incremented, alert NOT fired, all state preserved ✅
  - Manual skipped run with `includeSkipped: true` → failure alert NOT emitted ✅

  Control-group tests confirm scheduled runs still drive all state effects normally.

- **What was not tested**: Live Gateway CLI `openclaw cron run` end-to-end (covered by earlier Docker CLI proof at `642c3450d9` — subsequent commits were formatting + test coverage changes). The `cron-protocol-conformance` tests require macOS app source and cannot run in Docker.

### Manual-run state contract

`cron run` is a debug/verification command. Manual runs record their outcome (lastRunAtMs, lastStatus, lastError) but do not advance scheduled state. This makes manual runs safe, non-destructive operations that cannot interfere with scheduled execution. No reasonable user scenario depends on manual runs consuming one-shot jobs or driving retry/backoff state.

## Real behavior proof (Docker, HEAD `ccb89e3f11`, 2026-06-02)

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: `lastRunWasManual` field was missing from the `CronJobStateSchema` and `CronJobStatePatchSchema` in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.ts`. Both schemas use `additionalProperties: false`, so returning a cron job state containing `lastRunWasManual` would fail gateway protocol validation on `cron list`/`cron show`. Any cron job state object with `lastRunWasManual: true` (set by `timer.ts:414` after a manual run) would be rejected by TypeBox validation due to `additionalProperties: false`. The `CronJobStatePatchSchema` was similarly missing the field, preventing state patches that include it.

## Real behavior proof (Docker, HEAD `8596607fca`, 2026-06-02 — backoff fix)

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Manual `cron run` on a recurring job that errors must not open a backoff window that blocks the next scheduled fire. Previously, `isErrorBackoffPending()`, `resolveJobErrorBackoffUntilMs()`, `isPendingErrorBackoffSlot()`, and `recomputeJobNextRunAtMs()` read `lastRunStatus` and `lastRunAtMs` without checking `lastRunWasManual`, causing a manual error to push `nextRunAtMs` forward and block the timer-scheduled fire.

- **Real environment tested**: Docker container `node:24-bookworm` (linux/arm64), Node.js `v24.16.0`, Vitest `v4.1.7`, patched OpenClaw at commit `8596607fca`.

- **Failing proof before fix**: On upstream/main, `resolveJobErrorBackoffUntilMs()` does not check `lastRunWasManual`. A recurring every-job with `lastRunWasManual: true` and `lastRunStatus: "error"` would have `resolveJobErrorBackoffUntilMs()` return a backoff deadline, `isErrorBackoffPending()` would return `true`, and `isRunnableJob()` would return `false` — blocking the next scheduled fire. `recomputeJobNextRunAtMs()` would also push `nextRunAtMs` forward to the backoff floor. - **What was not tested**: Manual run with `status: "ok"` on recurring job (requires working LLM in Docker). Multi-node cluster, production load, actual delivery to chat channels.




## Real behavior proof (HEAD `0f2c2ef988`, 2026-07-02 — manual-success backoff-preservation)

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: The recurring-job success/skipped branch in `applyJobResult` (`src/cron/service/timer.ts`) recomputed `nextRunAtMs` unconditionally. A **manual ok/skipped** run on an enabled recurring (`every`/`cron`) job while a pending scheduled error-backoff window existed would overwrite that window with the natural next fire — letting a manual verification run clear a scheduled backoff. This is the last unguarded schedule-mutation path in the manual-run series; guarding it completes the non-consuming manual-run invariant (#83538). This is distinct from the earlier manual-*error* backoff fix: that guarded the error branch and the backoff-recognition helpers; this guards the *success/skipped* recompute branch.
- **Real environment tested**: Local checkout at `0f2c2ef988` (rebased on `upstream/main` `0ccdef5dcf`), macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, Vitest `v4`.
- **Failing proof before fix**: With the guard disabled (`false && opts?.isManual`), the new regression test fails — a manual ok run rewrites `nextRunAtMs` to the natural next fire (`endedAt + 60s`) instead of preserving the pending backoff window (`endedAt + 30min`), while the other regression tests still pass. Restoring the guard turns it green.

When manual, `nextRunAtMs` is left untouched (with an info log). When not manual, behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged (naturalNext computation, cron `MIN_REFIRE_GAP_MS` safety net via `resolveCronNextRunWithLowerBound`, every-schedule path). The disabled-job terminal `else { job.state.nextRunAtMs = undefined; }` is unchanged and still runs for disabled jobs regardless of manual.

```bash

node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/cron/service/timer.ts src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts

```

```
      Tests  81 passed (81)
```

- **New regression test**: `#83538: manual ok run on recurring job preserves pending scheduled error-backoff window` — sets up an `every` 60s job with a pending backoff window (`nextRunAtMs = endedAt + 30min`, `consecutiveErrors: 2`), runs a manual OK completion (`isManual: true`), and asserts the backoff `nextRunAtMs` is preserved (not reset to the natural next run). The job stays enabled with counter intact.
- **Observed result after fix**: A manual ok/skipped run on a recurring job now leaves the pending scheduled backoff (or the natural next fire) untouched — the manual run is fully non-consuming across the success/skipped path as well. Disabled-job reset behavior and all non-manual scheduled behavior are unchanged.
- **What was not tested**: Live Gateway CLI end-to-end for this specific success-path branch (a manual `ok` outcome requires a working LLM provider in Docker; earlier Docker CLI proofs cover the manual-run survival/backoff paths). target.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)
target.body:
Closes #97750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on any deployment that serves a Claude model through an anthropic-messages-compatible proxy would see raw tool-call XML in their chat replies, and sometimes get no usable answer at all, when the proxy intermittently degraded a native `tool_use` block into plain text.

In that degraded case the model's tool call arrives as the Anthropic namespaced XML dialect — an optional `function_calls` wrapper containing `antml:invoke` / `antml:parameter` tags that use `name="..."` attributes (MiniMax emits the same shape with an `mm:` prefix). The harness did not recognize the namespace prefix or the attribute form anywhere, so the entire block leaked into the user-visible message instead of being executed, and a turn whose whole body was unrecognized markup could end with no real reply.

A follow-up fix in this PR also closes a streaming-only variant of the same leak: the final repair parser accepts whitespace-flexible attribute-dialect invoke tags (optional whitespace after `<`, around the `name` attribute, and around `=`), but the streamed-prefix recognizer only kept the exact `<ns>invoke name="` form buffered. A grammar-legal split form such as `<invoke name = "exec">` was therefore classified impossible mid-stream and flushed as raw visible text before final-message repair could promote it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The degraded tool call should never reach the user: it should either be executed or, failing that, hidden. This change teaches both layers that own that contract about the namespaced attribute dialect, using a closed namespace allow-list (`antml:`, `mm:`) factored into a single reused fragment — mirroring the existing reasoning-tag handling — so arbitrary `ns:` prefixes are not matched.

- Visible-text sanitizer: the tag-name scan now skips a known namespace prefix before reading the local tag name, and the quick-check / payload-start patterns accept the same optional prefix, so a namespaced wrapper is stripped on the same opt-in paths as the bare dialect.
- Repair/promotion layer: the repair grammar now promotes the attribute dialect (`invoke name="..."` / `parameter name="..."`, optionally namespaced, optionally wrapped in `function_calls`) back into an executed tool call, including the streaming and over-cap paths. Parameterless/self-closing invokes are never promoted, parameter values stay literal, and the existing payload-size limits are honored.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: `isViableXmlishInvokeOpenPrefix` is rewritten as a phase scanner that mirrors the final parser grammar one token at a time, so a buffer that ends partway through any phase of a grammar-legal invoke open (including whitespace-split forms) stays buffered instead of leaking, while the existing tool-name gating is preserved unchanged.
- `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` gained an optional code-region predicate, threaded in from the delivery pipeline and `sanitizeUserFacingText`, so a complete invoke block inside a fenced or inline code span is no longer silently removed.

Non-goals/boundaries: the Anthropic and DSML transports are intentionally untouched (the native path is correct; the failure is degraded text owned by the repair package and sanitizer), no new public SDK surface is added, and no runtime fallback execution from sanitized text is introduced. The equals dialect (`<function=...>`/`<parameter=...>`), bracket, and Harmony paths are unchanged.

## User Impact

Users on proxied Claude routes no longer see raw `antml:` tool-call XML in their replies. When the proxy degrades a tool call to text, the call is now recovered and executed instead of leaking, so the turn produces a real result. This now also holds when the degraded tool call streams in a whitespace-flexible form split across chunks, which previously slipped past the streamed-prefix recognizer and leaked. Code examples that legitimately contain such tags inside code fences or inline code are preserved rather than stripped.

## Evidence

Focused unit tests cover both layers and the edge cases:

- Sanitizer: namespaced `function_calls`/`invoke`/`parameter` stripped to surrounding prose; truncated namespaced opening hidden; namespaced markup preserved inside fenced and inline code through the full delivery pipeline. Delivery-path regression coverage locks both directions across the `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare (no-namespace) prefixes: an unfenced standalone `invoke` block (and a pure standalone block with no surrounding prose) is stripped, while the same block inside a fenced code span is preserved verbatim, so the real leak shape is removed without over-scrubbing legitimate code examples.
- Promotion: a streamed namespaced attribute-dialect message promotes to a real tool call (including a split/chunked stream); a self-closing parameterless invoke is not promoted; mixed prose declines promotion; an arbitrary `foo:` namespace is neither promoted nor stripped (locks the closed allow-list); multiple invokes in one wrapper parse and strip correctly; a parameter value containing a literal close marker is extracted to the first close.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: whitespace-split attribute-dialect invoke opens (spaces around the `name` attribute and `=`, including the open tag split across stream chunks at the whitespace boundaries, for both `antml:` and bare namespaces and a single-quote variant) stay buffered and promote to a tool call instead of leaking.

Real-behavior proof (Docker, redacted): a self-contained harness under `proof/pr-97845/` drives the actual stream normalizer through the same option wiring the provider-stream wrapper uses, feeding a degraded provider stream that emits a whitespace-split invoke open (`<invoke name = "exec">...`) split across chunks at the whitespace boundaries. Captured runtime output shows the regression and its fix:

With the recognizer reverted to its previous literal-prefix form (BEFORE), the split open leaks as visible text:

```
fake upstream chunks: ["<invoke"," name"," ="," \"exec\">","<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>","</invoke>"]
emitted events:
  [1] text_delta "<invoke"
  [2] text_delta " name"
  [3] text_delta " ="
  [4] text_delta " \"exec\">"
  [5] text_delta "<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>"
  [6] text_delta "</invoke>"
  [7] toolcall_start ...
visible text emitted to user: "<invoke name = \"exec\"><parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter></invoke>"
VERDICT: LEAK
```

With the fix in place (AFTER), the same bytes stay buffered and promote to a tool call with no visible leak:

```
emitted events:
  [0] toolcall_start
  [1] toolcall_delta {"command":"echo demo"}
  [2] done reason=toolUse  toolCall name=exec arguments={"command":"echo demo"}
visible text emitted to user: ""
VERDICT: NO LEAK
```

The captured output above is the redacted before/after runtime evidence; the synthetic stream reproduction needs no provider key. (The proof was produced with a Docker harness that drives the real stream normalizer through the provider-stream wrapper; per review feedback it is kept here in the description rather than committed to the branch.)

Local validation:

```
node scripts/test-projects.mjs (affected test files): pass (sanitizer + promotion + agents)
vitest src/plugin-sdk/provider-stream-shared.test.ts: 70 pass (incl. new whitespace-split regression)
pnpm tsgo:core && pnpm tsgo:core:test: clean
oxlint on changed source files: 0 warnings, 0 errors
oxfmt --check on changed files: all correctly formatted
```

target.title: fix(discord): add defensive JSON.parse wrappers to gateway and migration stores
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: Two JSON.parse call sites in the Discord extension lack defensive wrappers. Malformed or non-JSON input can throw bare SyntaxErrors that crash the gateway metadata fetch or the legacy state migration, without actionable diagnostics.

**Solution**: Add try-catch guards that preserve error context. Gateway metadata parse errors get a descriptive message. Migration store parse errors are thrown with a clear message while file I/O errors (ENOENT/EACCES) propagate naturally to the shared migration runner for proper reporting.

**What changed**: 
- `gateway-metadata.ts:159-164` — JSON.parse wrapped in try-catch, throws `"Discord gateway metadata response is not valid JSON"` on parse failure.
- `model-picker-preferences-migrations.ts:53-64` — Separated fs.readFileSync from JSON.parse. Parse errors throw a clear `"Corrupted legacy Discord thread bindings store: file is not valid JSON"`. I/O errors (ENOENT/EACCES) propagate to the shared runner.
- Two new regression tests covering both malformed-input paths.

**What did NOT change**:
- Function signatures (parseDiscordGatewayInfoBody returns APIGatewayBotInfo, readLegacyThreadBindingsStore returns LegacyThreadBindingsStore).
- Valid JSON behavior at either call site.
- Any other file, dependency, config, or build surface.

## What Problem This Solves

The defensive programming audit (section 1.3) identified two remaining locations in the Discord extension where JSON.parse is called without try-catch protection. Malformed or non-JSON input at these call sites can throw untyped SyntaxErrors that crash the gateway metadata fetch or the legacy state migration process.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Defensive JSON.parse wrappers for Discord gateway metadata (parseDiscordGatewayInfoBody) and legacy thread-bindings migration (readLegacyThreadBindingsStore).

**Real environment tested**: Local development environment, Node 24, Linux x64.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Gateway metadata path:
```
$ npx tsx -e "
import { parseDiscordGatewayInfoBody } from './extensions/discord/src/monitor/gateway-metadata.js';
// Malformed JSON
try { parseDiscordGatewayInfoBody('not valid json'); } catch (e) { console.log('Malformed JSON:', String(e)); }
// HTML input (simulating Discord API 502)
try { parseDiscordGatewayInfoBody('<html>502 Bad Gateway</html>'); } catch (e) { console.log('HTML input:', String(e)); }
// Valid input
try { const r = parseDiscordGatewayInfoBody(JSON.stringify({url:'wss://gateway.discord.gg/',shards:1,session_start_limit:{total:1000,remaining:999,reset_after:5000,max_concurrency:1}})); console.log('Valid input: url =', r.url); } catch (e) { console.log('Valid input error:', e); }
"
```

Migration path (corrupted file → clear parse error):
```
$ npx tsx -e "
import { detectDiscordLegacyStateMigrations } from './extensions/discord/src/monitor/model-picker-preferences-migrations.js';
import fs from 'node:fs/promises';
import os from 'node:os';
import path from 'node:path';
const dir = await fs.mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'ev-'));
await fs.mkdir(path.join(dir, 'discord'), { recursive: true });
await fs.writeFile(path.join(dir, 'discord', 'thread-bindings.json'), 'not valid json');
const plans = await detectDiscordLegacyStateMigrations({cfg:{},env:{},oauthDir:path.join(dir,'credentials'),stateDir:dir});
try { plans[0].readEntries(); } catch (e) { console.log('Corrupted JSON:', String(e)); }
"
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
Gateway metadata:
- Malformed JSON:       ✅ Error: Discord gateway metadata response is not valid JSON
- HTML input (502):     ✅ Error: Discord gateway metadata response is not valid JSON
- Valid metadata:       ✅ Parsed successfully, url: wss://gateway.discord.gg/

Migration:
- Corrupted JSON:       ✅ Error: Corrupted legacy Discord thread bindings store: file is not valid JSON
- Valid JSON:           ✅ Parsed successfully, entries: 1
- Missing file:         ✅ No plans created (no crash)

Tests:
- model-picker-preferences-migrations: 1 file, 8 tests passed
- gateway-metadata:                     1 file, 3 tests passed
```

**Observed result after the fix**: Malformed inputs at both call sites now produce descriptive, actionable error messages instead of bare SyntaxErrors or silent null returns. Valid inputs continue to work identically. The migration runner preserves the actual read/parse error cause for doctor warnings.

**What was not tested**: Full end-to-end gateway startup with a real Discord token was not tested (no real token in dev environment). A full doctor migration run was not performed. Both changes are additive guarding of existing bare JSON.parse calls and do not affect any other code paths.

## Risk checklist

- [x] **merge-risk: 🚨 compatibility** — Low. The migration hunk previously returned null for I/O errors, hiding the root cause. The fix preserves the original throw behavior for I/O errors so the shared runner reports the actual cause. Valid migration paths are unaffected. Mitigation: focused regression tests cover both parse-failure and valid-input paths.
- [x] **merge-risk: 🚨 session-state** — Low. Discord thread bindings are session/routing state. The migration hunk only changes how corrupted legacy binding errors are reported — doctor now shows the real error instead of a generic validation message. Mitigation: both new and existing migration tests pass.
- [x] AI-assisted development was used to generate this PR body and implement the fix.

target.title: feat(minimax): opt M3 into MiniMax priority lane via fastMode
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

MiniMax-M3 exposes a paid low-latency `service_tier: "priority"` lane on its
Anthropic-compatible endpoint, but OpenClaw has no way to opt a model's
requests into it. Operators running latency-sensitive M3 workloads cannot
trade spend for the faster lane today.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gate the priority lane behind the existing per-model `fastMode` flag, in the
**MiniMax-owned fast-mode wrapper** (`createMinimaxFastModeWrapper`). That
wrapper is the canonical fast-mode path: it already receives `DynamicFastMode`
and resolves it per stream call (via `resolveBooleanFastMode`), so it handles
the function form `/fast auto` passes, not just a literal `true`. For M2.7 it
rewrites to the highspeed model variant; for M3 (which has no highspeed
variant) it now injects `service_tier: "priority"`.

The MiniMax plugin wires this wrapper itself, passing a **plugin-owned cost
resolver**, instead of the generic `minimax-fast-mode` stream-family shortcut.
Pricing therefore stays plugin-owned and core stays provider-pricing-free.
Because the bundled provider was that deprecated shortcut's only consumer, this
revision removes the now-orphaned `MINIMAX_FAST_MODE_STREAM_HOOKS` seam rather
than leave a divergent, billing-incomplete second path.

Scope and non-goals:

- Opt-in only. Default behavior is unchanged when `fastMode` is unset/false.
- M3 only. M2.x models route to the highspeed variant instead and gain no
  priority `service_tier`.
- A `service_tier` already set by an earlier wrapper or caller is preserved.

## User Impact

Operators can opt MiniMax-M3 requests into MiniMax's priority lane by setting
`fastMode` (`/fast on`, `/fast auto`, or `params.fastMode: true`) on the model,
reducing latency at higher cost, and OpenClaw's cost estimate now matches the
billed lane. No impact on any model or caller that does not enable fast mode.

## Evidence

This revision is **rebased onto latest `main`** and resolves the review
findings plus the follow-up cleanup:

- **[BLOCKER] Priority/highspeed cost is reflected in estimates.** Opting M3
  into `service_tier: priority` previously kept standard M3 pricing, and the
  M2.7 highspeed rewrite kept standard M2.7 pricing. The fast-mode wrapper now
  bills the lane it actually runs: `createMinimaxFastModeWrapper` gained an
  optional `resolveFastLaneCost`, the wrapper picks the lane and the **MiniMax
  plugin owns the pricing** (core stays provider-pricing free). M3 priority
  bills **1.5x** the standard rate per
  [MiniMax pricing](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/guides/pricing-paygo);
  M2.7 highspeed bills the highspeed variant's rate. Mirrors the OpenAI
  service-tier multiplier approach in `openai-responses.ts`.
- **[IMPORTANT] Docs.** `docs/providers/minimax.md`, `docs/gateway/config-tools.md`,
  `docs/concepts/model-providers.md`, `docs/tools/slash-commands.md`,
  `docs/tools/thinking.md`, and `docs/plugins/sdk-provider-plugins.md` now
  describe M3 priority processing, `/fast auto`, the 1.5x pricing, and the
  affected provider IDs.
- **[IMPORTANT] Registration coverage.** `extensions/minimax/index.test.ts`
  proves the M3 `service_tier: priority` + 1.5x cost path through the real
  registered provider hook for **both** `minimax` and `minimax-portal`.
- **[NIT] Tier value.** The preservation test uses MiniMax's own `standard`
  tier value instead of Anthropic's `standard_only`.
- **[cleanup] Dropped the orphaned `minimax-fast-mode` SDK family seam.** Since
  the plugin now wires its own hook, the deprecated `MINIMAX_FAST_MODE_STREAM_HOOKS`
  export, the `minimax-fast-mode` family member/case, its stream-matrix test
  coverage, and the families-table doc row are removed. Regenerated the plugin
  SDK API baseline and re-pinned the public surface budget for the net export
  change (`resolveBooleanFastMode` is now exported and the `ResolveMinimaxFastLaneCost`
  type added; `+2` public exports / `+2` callable after dropping the deprecated
  hook). Also corrected the M3 priority-cost comment so its example matches the
  billed rate (`$0.60/$2.40 -> $0.90/$3.60`).

**Validation** (all local, rebased onto latest `main`):

```
pnpm test src/llm/providers/stream-wrappers/minimax.test.ts   → 22 passed
pnpm test extensions/minimax/index.test.ts                    → 15 passed
pnpm test src/plugin-sdk/provider-stream.test.ts              →  8 passed
pnpm test test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts      →  8 passed
tsgo:core:test / tsgo:extensions:test                         → clean
pnpm build                                                    → clean (no INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT)
oxfmt --check / plugin-sdk:api:check / surface-report --check → clean
```

The registration test drives the exact hooks the MiniMax extension registers
for both provider IDs and captures the outgoing payload + billed cost:

- `MiniMax-M2.7` + fast mode → request model `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` (both
  `minimax` and `minimax-portal`)
- `MiniMax-M3` + fast mode → outgoing `service_tier: "priority"` and model cost
  scaled to 1.5x (`{0.6,2.4,0.12,0}` → `{0.9,3.6,0.18,0}`) for both
  `minimax` and `minimax-portal`

**Live endpoint proof.** Real MiniMax-M3 requests to
`https://api.minimax.io/anthropic/v1/messages` (API key redacted), showing the
served lane MiniMax echoes back in `usage.service_tier`:

```
# control — no service_tier
  request:  {"model":"MiniMax-M3","max_tokens":16,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"ping"}]}
  HTTP 200  → usage.service_tier = "standard"

# with the flag this PR sets
  request:  {"model":"MiniMax-M3","max_tokens":16,"messages":[...],"service_tier":"priority"}
  HTTP 200  → usage.service_tier = "priority"
  response: {"type":"message","model":"MiniMax-M3","content":[{"type":"text","text":"🏓 Pong! ..."}],
             "usage":{"input_tokens":50,"output_tokens":12,"service_tier":"priority"},"stop_reason":"end_turn"}
```

The live endpoint accepts `service_tier: "priority"` for MiniMax-M3 and confirms
the request was served on the priority lane (`usage.service_tier: "priority"`),
versus `"standard"` with the flag off — the exact before/after this PR's
`fastMode` flag produces.
